loading_messages.description: 1–4 loading messages shown to the user while the visual renders, each roughly 5 words long. Write them in the same language the user is using. Use 1 for simple visuals, more for complex ones. If the topic is serious — illness, disease, pandemics, death, grief, war, conflict, poverty, disaster, trauma, abuse, addiction, medical decisions, politically charged subjects, or anything where the reader might be personally affected — keep these BORING: describe what the code is doing in the dullest generic way, no jargon-as-drama, no evocative terms. Pandemic growth model — NOT ['Simulating patient zero', 'Modeling the curve'] (documentary-narrator voice), YES ['Setting up the model', 'Running the calculation']. Cancer timeline — NOT ['Charting the battle ahead'], YES ['Laying out the stages']. If you have to ask whether it's serious, it is. Otherwise, have fun — reach for alliteration, puns, personification, wordplay, whatever lands in that language. Playful examples — revenue chart: ['Bribing bars to stand taller', 'Asking Q4 where it went']; kanban: ['Herding cards into columns', 'Dragging, dropping, not stopping'].

title.description: Short snake_case identifier for this visual. Must be specific and disambiguating — if the conversation has multiple visuals, this title alone should tell you which one is being referenced (e.g. 'q4_revenue_by_product_line' not 'chart', 'oauth_login_flow' not 'diagram'). Also used as the download filename, so no spaces or special characters.

widget_code.description: SVG or HTML code to render. For SVG: raw SVG code starting with <svg> tag, must use CSS variables for colors. Example: <svg viewBox="0 0 700 400" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg">...</svg>. For HTML: raw HTML content to render, do NOT include DOCTYPE, <html>, <head>, or <body> tags. Use CSS variables for theming. Keep background transparent and avoid top-level padding. Scripts are supported but execute after streaming completes.

English

Front-End Technical Test � Multi-Country
Car Insurance

Test objective

This test measures your ability to build software with an AI-driven development flow, not
just your ability to code. You will build a multi-country car insurance quoting app with
Angular and Strapi, and what matters most is how you design, operate and control the AI
system that helps you do it.

There is no single "correct" flow we expect. You decide which agents, subagents and skills
to use, in what order, and at which points a person steps in. We evaluate whether your
decisions are explicit, justified, traceable and repeatable.

Using AI tools is allowed and required.

Business context

An insurtech that sells digital insurance in Colombia and Chile wants to launch a car
insurance product with a single front-end application that can sell in both countries.

The business team, which is not technical, must be able to change the form fields and the
offered plans from Strapi without requesting a deployment. Each country has its own
regulations, identity documents, currency, coverages and copy, so the content the app
consumes changes by country.

Part of the challenge is for you to propose and justify the strategy for differentiating
content by country in Strapi and in Angular.

Functional scope

The application is a wizard with at least 3 steps. You may add more if you justify it.

Step Screen         What it must do

1        Data form  Captures policyholder and vehicle data. Fields,
                    types, validations, copy and order are configured in
2        Plan list  Strapi per country.

                    Shows the plans available for the country with
                    price, coverages and benefits, configured in Strapi.
                    The user picks one.

                                                                                        Page 1 of 9
 English

Step Screen                 What it must do

3        Summary and payment Shows the entered data and the chosen plan, and

                            offers the option to pay.

The scope rules are:

     The same application and the same build serve Colombia and Chile.
     Changing a form field or a plan in Strapi must be reflected in the app without
     changing code.
     Price calculation may be simulated: a real rating engine is not expected.
     Payment is simulated: a button that leads to a confirmation screen or a mock gateway.
     Do not integrate real payment gateways or use real card data.
     Use fictitious data only.
     Use a front-end strategy to persist the data; a database is not required.

The functional detail of each screen is in the user stories at the end of this document.

Technical requirements

Topic          Requirement

Front end      Angular 21 or later: standalone components,
               signals, built-in control flow ( @if , @for ), no
               NgModules

Content backend Strapi 5 or later

Forms          Step 1 form generated dynamically from the Strapi
               configuration, with typed validations

Multi-country  Content differentiation strategy by country,
               proposed by you and documented in an ADR

Security       No Strapi token with write permissions may reach
               the browser. Public role permissions minimal and
               justified

Testing        Unit tests for the relevant logic and at least one
               e2e test of the full flow for one country

Environment    The whole project starts with a single command
               (for example docker compose up ), with seed data
               for both countries

                                                                              Page 2 of 9
 English

Topic          Requirement
Accessibility
               The wizard can be completed using only the
Responsive     keyboard, and fields have accessible labels
               Works on mobile and desktop

List in the README any requirement you decide not to meet and why.

Agentic flow requirements

The expected solution is an agentic flow: a system of AI agents that takes the user stories
to QA-ready code, with people stepping in at the points you define. We do not give you
the order or composition of the flow; designing it is part of the test.

Mandatory requirements:

     Subagents. The flow uses subagents with separate responsibilities. Their definitions
     (instructions, allowed tools, inputs and outputs) are versioned in the repository.
     Skills. The flow uses at least one custom skill, versioned in the repository, that
     encapsulates reusable project knowledge (for example conventions, templates or
     procedures).
     Context file. There is a global context file ( AGENTS.md , CLAUDE.md or equivalent)
     with the conventions all agents must follow.
     ADRs. Relevant architecture decisions are recorded in ADRs (MADR, Nygard or
     similar format), with context, alternatives considered and consequences. At minimum,
     one on the multi-country strategy.
     Specs. Each user story has its spec before it is implemented.
     Code review. There is evidence of code review within the flow, with findings and how
     they were resolved.
     Traceability. The thread user story  spec  ADR  code  tests  review can be
     followed.

We suggest, though it is not mandatory, using Spec-Driven Development (SDD): the spec
is the source of truth and the code is derived from it. You may use an SDD framework (for
example Spec Kit, Kiro or another) or your own variant, but explain why.

The tool is your choice: Claude Code, Cursor, GitHub Copilot, OpenCode, Codex or
another. Justify your choice.

                                                                    Page 3 of 9
 English

Step by step: from functional user story to QA handoff

You must deliver a FLOW.md file that explains your full flow, from receiving a functional
user story until the increment is ready for QA. Include a diagram of the flow (Mermaid or
image).

For each step of the flow, document at least the following:

Step     Description   AI     AI, agent,         Deliverable produced Human in the loop
                       used?  subagent or skill
Step     What happens         used
name     and why
                       Yes /  Tool, model and    File or artifact       Who steps in, what they
                       No     component          produced (path in the  review or approve, and
                                                 repo)                  what happens on
                                                                        rejection

This table is only the minimum format: you define the number, order and content of the
steps.

Also, in FLOW.md briefly answer:

     What you would do differently if a team of 5 developers used this flow.
     Which part of the flow did not work as expected and how you adjusted it.
     At which points you decided not to use AI and why.

Deliverables and rules

Deliver a Git repository, public or private and shared with whoever sent you the test. It
must contain:

     The Angular application code and the Strapi project, with seed data for Colombia and
     Chile.
      README.md with instructions to run the project and any requirements not met.
      FLOW.md with the step by step of the agentic flow and its diagram.
     A global context file ( AGENTS.md , CLAUDE.md or equivalent).
     Versioned subagent and skill definitions.
     A specs folder, at least one spec per user story.
     An ADRs folder, with at least the multi-country strategy ADR.
     Evidence of code reviews (reports, PR comments or similar) and how they were
     resolved.
     Unedited logs or exports of your sessions with the agents.

Rules:

                                                                                         Page 4 of 9
 English

         Use fictitious data only. Do not include real personal data or credentials in the
         repository.

         If a tool requires a paid plan and you don't have access, use a free alternative and say
         so.

Evaluation criteria

65% of the score covers the agentic flow and its artifacts; 35% covers the application.

Criterion                      What we look at                               Weight

Agentic flow design            Clear responsibilities per subagent,          20%
                               defined inputs and outputs, skills with real
                               value, a context file that governs
                               generation

Human in the loop and control  Justified checkpoints, approval or            15%

                               rejection criteria, evidence that the person

                               corrected the agent

Specs and ADRs                 Specs that detect gaps in the user story      15%

                               and make it verifiable; ADRs with real

                               alternatives and consequences

Review and verification        Real findings in reviews, traceable fixes,    15%

                               tests that validate behavior

Multi-country strategy and     Content differentiated by country without 15%
configurability                duplicating the app; form and plans 100%
                               configurable from Strapi

Angular and Strapi technical quality Modern Angular, typing, loading and error 10%
                                                       state handling, token and permission
                                                       security

Communication                  Clarity of FLOW.md and README                 10%

Functional user stories

These are the three input stories for your flow, one per screen.

US-01 � Policyholder and vehicle data form

Story

                                                                             Page 5 of 9
 English

As a person interested in insuring my car, I want to enter my data and my vehicle's data in a
simple form, so that I receive insurance options suited to my country and my vehicle.
Context
Fields change by country. In Colombia the identity document is usually the citizenship ID
(c�dula de ciudadan�a) or foreigner ID (c�dula de extranjer�a), and the vehicle is identified
by its license plate (placa). In Chile the document is the RUT and the vehicle is identified
by its license plate (patente). The business team wants to add, remove or reorder fields
from Strapi without asking development for changes.
Business rules

     Each field is configured in Strapi with: label, type (text, number, select, date,
     checkbox), required flag, validations, help text, error message, order and country.
     Select fields (for example, make or city) get their options from Strapi.
     The vehicle year cannot be later than next year or more than 20 years old.
     The policyholder must be of legal age.
Acceptance criteria

  Scenario: Form configured by country
      Given fields are configured in Strapi for Colombia and for Chile
      When I open the application in the context of a country
      Then I see only the fields configured for that country, in the defined

  order

  Scenario: Field validation
      Given I am filling out the form
      When a field does not meet its configured validation
      Then I see the configured error message next to the field
      And I cannot move to the next step

  Scenario: Configuration change without deployment
      Given the business team adds a new published field in Strapi
      When I reload the application
      Then the new field appears without code changes

  Scenario: Keep data when going back
      Given I moved on to step 2
      When I go back to step 1
      Then my data is still filled in

US-02 � Plan list

Story

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              Page 6 of 9
 English

As a person getting a quote, I want to see the plans available for my country with their
price and coverages, so that I can choose the one that best fits my needs.
Context
Plans, coverages, benefits and prices change by country and are managed by the
business team from Strapi. The business team wants to highlight one plan as
"recommended" and control the order in which plans appear.
Business rules

     Each plan is configured in Strapi with: name, short description, base price, currency,
     coverages, benefits, order, recommended flag, active status and country.
     Only published and active plans for the country are shown.
     The price is shown in the country's currency and format (Colombian pesos or Chilean
     pesos).
     The final price may be adjusted by a simulated rule based on the step 1 data. The rule
     is documented.
     Only one plan can be selected.
Acceptance criteria

  Scenario: Plans for the country
      Given I completed the step 1 form
      When I reach the plans step
      Then I see only the active and published plans for my country, in the

  configured order

  Scenario: Recommended plan
      Given a plan is marked as recommended in Strapi
      When I view the plan list
      Then that plan is visually distinguished from the others

  Scenario: Plan selection
      Given I am on the plan list
      When I select a plan
      Then it is marked as chosen
      And I can move on to the summary

  Scenario: No plans available
      Given there are no active plans for my country
      When I reach the plans step
      Then I see a message explaining that no plans are available

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              Page 7 of 9
 English

US-03 � Summary and payment

Story
As a person who chose a plan, I want to review a summary of my quote and pay, so that I
become insured.
Context
Before paying, the person must confirm their data and accept the terms and conditions,
whose text varies by country and is managed by the business team from Strapi. Payment
is simulated for this test.
Business rules

     The summary shows the policyholder's data, the vehicle's data and the chosen plan
     with its final price.
     The document number is shown partially masked.
     From the summary the person can go back to edit their data or change the plan.
     The pay button is enabled only after accepting the terms and conditions.
     The payment cannot be submitted twice.
     On successful payment, a confirmation with a simulated quote number is shown.
Acceptance criteria

  Scenario: Complete summary
      Given I chose a plan
      When I reach the summary
      Then I see my data, my vehicle's data and the chosen plan with its final

  price

  Scenario: Terms by country
      Given I am on the summary
      When I view the terms and conditions
      Then the text matches the one configured in Strapi for my country
      And the pay button is disabled until I accept them

  Scenario: Successful payment
      Given I accepted the terms
      When I click pay
      Then the button is locked while the payment is processed
      And I see the confirmation with the quote number

  Scenario: Rejected payment

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              Page 8 of 9
 English

      Given the simulated payment fails
      When I click pay
      Then I see a clear error message
      And I can try again without losing my information

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              Page 9 of 9

I read all 9 pages. Here is what I extracted, followed by my opinion and the gaps I found.

## What the test is really about

- **Weighting:** 65% is the agentic flow and its artifacts, and 35% is the app. The AI system is the product, and the quoting app is its output.
- **Scoring:** The flow must be explicit, justified, traceable and repeatable, and a person must step in at defined points. They also want evidence that you corrected the agent.
- **Weights:**

| Criterion | Weight |
|---|---|
| Agentic flow design | 20% |
| Human in the loop | 15% |
| Specs and ADRs | 15% |
| Review and verification | 15% |
| Multi-country strategy and configurability | 15% |
| Angular and Strapi quality | 10% |
| Communication (FLOW.md, README) | 10% |

## Mandatory deliverables checklist

- Angular 21+ app (standalone, signals, `@if`/`@for`, no NgModules) and a Strapi 5+ project, with seed data for CO and CL.
- One command to start everything, such as `docker compose up`.
- `README.md` with run instructions and a list of requirements you chose not to meet, with reasons.
- `FLOW.md` with a Mermaid or image diagram and the step table (step, description, AI used?, agent/subagent/skill, deliverable path, human in the loop and what happens on rejection). It must also answer three questions:
  - What would change for a team of 5 developers?
  - What didn't work as expected, and how did you adjust?
  - Where did you choose not to use AI, and why?
- `AGENTS.md` or `CLAUDE.md` as the global context file.
- Versioned subagent definitions (instructions, allowed tools, inputs, outputs) and at least one custom skill.
- A specs folder with at least one spec per user story, written before implementation.
- An ADRs folder with at least the multi-country ADR. It needs real alternatives and consequences.
- Code review evidence with findings and how they were resolved.
- **Unedited** session logs or exports.
- Justification for your tool choice, and for your SDD framework if you use one.
- Traceability from user story to spec, ADR, code, tests and review.

## Technical constraints that are easy to forget

- No Strapi write token may reach the browser, and Public role permissions must be minimal and justified.
- Unit tests plus at least one e2e test of the full flow for one country.
- The same build serves both countries.
- The wizard must work by keyboard only, fields need accessible labels, and the layout must be responsive.
- Fictitious data only, with no real card data or real gateways.
- Persistence is front-end only.
- If a tool needs a paid plan you don't have, use a free alternative and say so.

## Things in the user stories that are easy to miss

- **US-01:**
  - Field config attributes are label, type (text, number, select, date, checkbox), required, validations, help text, error message, order and country.
  - Select options come from Strapi.
  - Vehicle year can't be later than next year or more than 20 years old.
  - The policyholder must be of legal age.
  - Back navigation preserves data.
  - A new published field must appear on reload with no code change.
- **US-02:**
  - Plan attributes are name, description, base price, currency, coverages, benefits, order, recommended flag, active status and country.
  - Only published and active plans for the country are shown.
  - Prices use COP or CLP formatting.
  - Plans get a simulated price adjustment, and the rule must be documented.
  - Selecting a plan is single-select.
  - You need an empty state for no plans.
- **US-03:**
  - The summary shows the policyholder, the vehicle and the plan with its final price.
  - The document number is partially masked.
  - The person can go back to edit data or change the plan.
  - Terms and conditions text comes from Strapi per country.
  - The pay button is disabled until the terms are accepted, and it locks during processing (no double submit).
  - Success shows a simulated quote number.
  - A failed payment shows a clear error and the person can retry without losing data.

## What I think

**1. The brief rewards process over product, so the process needs to be visible from commit one.** The unedited logs and the evidence that you corrected the agent are only credible if we record them as we go. We should start logging now, before the first agent runs.

**2. The central design decision is the multi-country strategy.** Content differentiation in Strapi has three main options:
- Strapi i18n locales (`es-CO`, `es-CL`).
- A `country` relation or enum field on each content type.
- Separate Single/Collection types per country.

The brief says "country" and "locale" are not the same thing, and the stories only filter by country. A `country` relation with a Country collection is probably the most honest design, because it carries currency, document types and terms. I'd put it in the ADR with the alternatives. I haven't validated this yet, so it's a starting point for us to test.

**3. How the app learns its country is unspecified.** The brief says "in the context of a country" but never says how. The options are a URL segment (`/co`, `/cl`), a subdomain, or a selector. A URL segment is simplest for one build serving both countries and is easy to e2e test. This needs a decision and an ADR.

## Gaps and ambiguities to resolve in the specs

The brief says specs should "detect gaps in the user story," so these are good material for that.

- **Validations are underspecified.** The brief doesn't say how Strapi expresses them (regex, min/max, a named validator?). Age and vehicle year are relative to today, so they can't be static values. We'd need a dynamic rule type, such as `maxYearsAgo`, or the vehicle-year rule can't be configured without code.
- **RUT validation (check digit) and Colombian ID formats** are not defined. Are they config-driven or hardcoded?
- **Does the document type select change which fields show?** For example, cédula de ciudadanía versus cédula de extranjería. The brief doesn't mention conditional fields.
- **"Legal age"** is 18 in both countries, but it should be configurable.
- **The simulated price rule** is left entirely to us. It must be deterministic, documented and tested.
- **Draft versus published** in Strapi 5 needs care. The Public role should see only published content.
- **"Reflected without code changes"** means no caching that breaks the "reload and see it" scenario. Our caching and ISR choices must respect that.
- **"Keep data when going back"** is covered by the front-end persistence rule, but what about a page refresh? Session storage is likely, and the PII implications deserve a mention (fictitious data only).
- **The masking format** for the document number isn't defined.
- **The failed-payment scenario** needs a way to trigger it deterministically for the e2e test.
- **Where does "country" come from for the terms text?** It must be tied to the same context as the form.
- **Security model:** the browser should only hit read-only public endpoints. The question is whether to proxy through a BFF or use the Public role directly. Either is fine if we justify it.
- **A paid-tool trap:** the test says to use a free alternative if needed. We should check what is available for logs and exports in our chosen tool.

## Next steps I'd suggest

1. Pick the tool. Claude Code fits well: subagents, skills and `CLAUDE.md` map directly to the requirements.
2. Decide the SDD approach (our own variant versus Spec Kit).
3. Decide the country-context strategy.
4. Set up session logging.

Tell me your thoughts and where you want to start. I'll keep tracking anything we haven't covered.

# Project Constitution


## 1. Engineering Principles

- **KISS & Pragmatic Reusability:** Keep solutions simple (KISS). Favor clear, specific code over premature abstractions; extract reusable pieces when a pattern repeats (Rule of Three) and genuinely reduces maintenance.
- **Intentional Naming:** Write code for human understanding. Names must express *what* something is or does, not *how*. Start functions with meaningful verbs and use clear nouns for variables.
- **Modular & Cohesive Files:** Avoid large, monolithic files. Split code into focused, single-responsibility components and functions.
- **Feature-First Architecture:** Organize folders and files by domain/feature rather than technical type to keep the repository clean and scalable.
- **Ask Before Over-engineering:** When facing trade-offs in complexity or architecture, pause and ask for alignment before introducing new abstractions or dependencies.
- **High-Value Testing:** Test business logic, validation rules, calculations, API integrations, data transformations, edge cases, and critical user interactions. Never write tests for CSS/styles, static layouts, configuration files, or initial scaffolding.
- **Atomic Conventional Commits:** Make small, atomic, and functional commits following the Conventional Commits specification; each commit must represent a complete, working unit.
- **BEM for CSS:** Follow the BEM (Block, Element, Modifier) methodology for CSS classes and HTML styling hooks.



## 2. Agentic Workflow Rules
- **Low Friction:** Keep `spec.md` and `plan.md` concise (maximum 150 lines each). No corporate fluff.
- **Autonomous Execution:** Once `plan.md` is approved, generate `tasks.md` and execute the implementation straight through without asking for confirmation between tasks.
- **Parallelism:** Use subagents (Agent tool) to execute independent tasks marked with `[P]` in `tasks.md` in parallel.
- **Self-Correction:** Run tests, typecheck, and linter after each block; automatically fix failures before reporting back to the user.

## 3. Human-in-the-Loop Boundaries (When to Stop and Ask)
Stop execution and ask for explicit approval ONLY if:
1. There are business ambiguities in `spec.md` (maximum 5 specific questions).
2. A new external dependency not included in the stack needs to be added.
3. There are breaking changes to public API contracts.
4. A test or build fails after 3 consecutive self-correction attempts.

# Project Constitution


## 1. Engineering Principles

- **KISS & Pragmatic Reusability:** Keep solutions simple (KISS). Favor clear, specific code over premature abstractions; extract reusable pieces when a pattern repeats (Rule of Three) and genuinely reduces maintenance.
- **Intentional Naming:** Write code for human understanding. Names must express *what* something is or does, not *how*. Start functions with meaningful verbs and use clear nouns for variables.
- **Modular & Cohesive Files:** Avoid large, monolithic files. Split code into focused, single-responsibility components and functions.
- **Feature-First Architecture:** Organize folders and files by domain/feature rather than technical type to keep the repository clean and scalable.
- **Ask Before Over-engineering:** When facing trade-offs in complexity or architecture, pause and ask for alignment before introducing new abstractions or dependencies.
- **High-Value Testing:** Test business logic, validation rules, calculations, API integrations, data transformations, edge cases, and critical user interactions. Never write tests for CSS/styles, static layouts, configuration files, or initial scaffolding.
- **Atomic Conventional Commits:** Make small, atomic, and functional commits following the Conventional Commits specification; each commit must represent a complete, working unit.
- **BEM for CSS:** Follow the BEM (Block, Element, Modifier) methodology for CSS classes and HTML styling hooks.

# Project Constitution


## 1. Engineering Principles

- **KISS & Pragmatic Reusability:** Keep solutions simple (KISS). Favor clear, specific code over premature abstractions; extract reusable pieces when a pattern repeats (Rule of Three) and genuinely reduces maintenance.
- **Intentional Naming:** Write code for human understanding. Names must express *what* something is or does, not *how*. Start functions with meaningful verbs and use clear nouns for variables.
- **Modular & Cohesive Files:** Avoid large, monolithic files. Split code into focused, single-responsibility components and functions.
- **Feature-First Architecture:** Organize folders and files by domain/feature rather than technical type to keep the repository clean and scalable.
- **Ask Before Over-engineering:** When facing trade-offs in complexity or architecture, pause and ask for alignment before introducing new abstractions or dependencies.
- **High-Value Testing:** Test business logic, validation rules, calculations, API integrations, data transformations, edge cases, and critical user interactions. Never write tests for CSS/styles, static layouts, configuration files, or initial scaffolding.
- **Atomic Conventional Commits:** Make small, atomic, and functional commits following the Conventional Commits specification; each commit must represent a complete, working unit.
- **BEM for CSS:** Follow the BEM (Block, Element, Modifier) methodology for CSS classes and HTML styling hooks.



## 2. Agentic Workflow Rules
- **Low Friction:** Keep `spec.md` and `plan.md` concise (maximum 150 lines each). No corporate fluff.
- **Autonomous Execution:** Once `plan.md` is approved, generate `tasks.md` and execute the implementation straight through without asking for confirmation between tasks.
- **Parallelism:** Use subagents (Agent tool) to execute independent tasks marked with `[P]` in `tasks.md` in parallel.
- **Self-Correction:** Run tests, typecheck, and linter after each block; automatically fix failures before reporting back to the user.

## 3. Human-in-the-Loop Boundaries (When to Stop and Ask)
Stop execution and ask for explicit approval ONLY if:
1. There are business ambiguities in `spec.md` (maximum 5 specific questions).
2. A new external dependency not included in the stack needs to be added.
3. There are breaking changes to public API contracts.
4. A test or build fails after 3 consecutive self-correction attempts.

# Project Constitution


## 1. Engineering Principles

- **KISS & Pragmatic Reusability:** Keep solutions simple (KISS). Favor clear, specific code over premature abstractions; extract reusable pieces when a pattern repeats (Rule of Three) and genuinely reduces maintenance.
- **Intentional Naming:** Write code for human understanding. Names must express *what* something is or does, not *how*. Start functions with meaningful verbs and use clear nouns for variables.
- **Modular & Cohesive Files:** Avoid large, monolithic files. Split code into focused, single-responsibility components and functions.
- **Feature-First Architecture:** Organize folders and files by domain/feature rather than technical type to keep the repository clean and scalable.
- **Ask Before Over-engineering:** When facing trade-offs in complexity or architecture, pause and ask for alignment before introducing new abstractions or dependencies.
- **High-Value Testing:** Test business logic, validation rules, calculations, API integrations, data transformations, edge cases, and critical user interactions. Never write tests for CSS/styles, static layouts, configuration files, or initial scaffolding.
- **Atomic Conventional Commits:** Make small, atomic, and functional commits following the Conventional Commits specification; each commit must represent a complete, working unit.
- **BEM for CSS:** Follow the BEM (Block, Element, Modifier) methodology for CSS classes and HTML styling hooks.



## 2. Agentic Workflow Rules
- **Low Friction:** Keep `spec.md` and `plan.md` concise (maximum 150 lines each). No corporate fluff.
- **Autonomous Execution:** Once `plan.md` is approved, generate `tasks.md` and execute the implementation straight through without asking for confirmation between tasks.
- **Parallelism:** Use subagents (Agent tool) to execute independent tasks marked with `[P]` in `tasks.md` in parallel.
- **Self-Correction:** Run tests, typecheck, and linter after each block; automatically fix failures before reporting back to the user.

## 3. Human-in-the-Loop Boundaries (When to Stop and Ask)
Stop execution and ask for explicit approval ONLY if:
1. There are business ambiguities in `spec.md` (maximum 5 specific questions).
2. A new external dependency not included in the stack needs to be added.
3. There are breaking changes to public API contracts.
4. A test or build fails after 3 consecutive self-correction attempts.

content.text:
Spec Kit, your workflow files and the stack are set up. Lint, typecheck, the unit tests and both builds pass. I couldn't start the stack with `docker compose up` because the Docker daemon is off, so that's still untested. Nothing is committed yet.

**What's in place**
- **Spec Kit:** installed for Claude Code with bash scripts (they run on Windows, Mac and Linux), so the `/speckit-*` skills are in `.claude/skills/`. To get it running I installed `uv` at user level.
- **Your workflow files**, word for word as you wrote them: [constitution.md](.specify/memory/constitution.md), [CLAUDE.md](CLAUDE.md) and the [autopilot skill](.claude/skills/autopilot/SKILL.md).
- **Angular 22.3** in `frontend/`. It already uses standalone components and Vitest, and I added:
  - strict TypeScript and strict template checks;
  - ESLint;
  - Playwright for the e2e test;
  - npm scripts `lint`, `typecheck`, `test`, `e2e` and `verify`. The autopilot can run `verify` after each wave.
- **Strapi 5.63** in `cms/`: TypeScript and SQLite, no example content.
- **[docker-compose.yml](docker-compose.yml)** runs Strapi and the built Angular app behind nginx. nginx forwards `/api` to Strapi, so the browser never needs a CMS address or a token. `ng serve` uses the same proxy locally. The Strapi secrets in it are placeholders marked dev-only, and the real `.env` is gitignored.

**Before you trust it, you should know**
- I added ESLint and Playwright without asking, which your constitution's "ask before a new dependency" rule covers. I took them as part of the stack: the self-correction loop needs a linter and the brief requires an e2e test.
- The first time Strapi runs, someone has to create the admin user by hand. The seed data and the Public role permissions still need to be built.
- `npm audit` reports 30 vulnerabilities in Strapi's dependencies. We should mention them in the README instead of forcing upgrades.

**Gaps between your flow and the brief:**
1. **Subagent definitions:** the brief requires them versioned, with instructions, allowed tools, inputs and outputs. Autopilot launches unnamed subagents, but nothing defines them in `.claude/agents/`. This is part of the 20% criterion.
2. **No code review step:** the brief requires review evidence with findings and how they were fixed (part of a 15% criterion). The autopilot ends with your reading of the summary. We should add a reviewer subagent that writes a report next to each spec.
3. **Human in the loop:** two gates are fine, but the brief also wants evidence that you corrected the agent. For each gate, FLOW.md must say what happens if you reject, including at your final summary review.
4. **ADRs aren't in the flow yet.** Gate 2 (Plan) is the natural place to create them.
5. **Traceability:** the brief wants to follow user story → spec → ADR → code → tests → review. We need IDs like US-01 in spec folders, commit messages and review reports.
6. **The context file has no stack rules:** CLAUDE.md only points to the constitution, which has no Angular or Strapi rules. I'd add a short stack section covering signals, `@if`/`@for`, no NgModules, no write token in the browser, and minimal Public permissions.
7. **FLOW.md needs material we can only collect now.** Write down what goes wrong and where you choose not to use AI as it happens, because the three FLOW.md questions need it.

When this conversation ends, I'll remind you to export it as Markdown into `ai-logs/`.

- speckit-analyze: Perform a non-destructive cross-artifact consistency and quality analysis across spec.md, plan.md, and tasks.md after task generation.
- speckit-checklist: Generate a custom checklist for the current feature based on user requirements.
- speckit-clarify: Identify underspecified areas in the current feature spec by asking up to 5 highly targeted clarification questions and encoding answers back into the spec.
- speckit-constitution: Create or update the project constitution from interactive or provided principle inputs.
- speckit-converge: Assess the current codebase against the feature's spec, plan, and tasks, then append any remaining unbuilt work as new tasks to tasks.md so implement can complete it.
- speckit-implement: Execute the implementation plan by processing and executing all tasks defined in tasks.md
- speckit-plan: Execute the implementation planning workflow using the plan template to generate design artifacts.
- speckit-specify: Create or update the feature specification from a natural language feature description.

content.text:
I've folded your seven answers into one proposal. Once you approve it I'll create everything in one pass: the agent files, the updated CLAUDE.md and autopilot, FLOW.md, and the `docs/` folders.

## 1. Subagents

The main session stays the orchestrator. It runs the Spec Kit skills, holds both gates, runs autopilot and makes the commits. Only the orchestrator commits, because parallel subagents committing at the same time would collide in git.

| Agent | What it does | Tools | Model | Gets | Produces |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `cms-developer` | Strapi content types, seed data, Public role permissions | Read, Write, Edit, Glob, Grep, Bash | Sonnet | task IDs, plus `spec.md` and `plan.md` | files in `cms/` and a short report |
| `frontend-developer` | Angular features and their unit tests | same | Sonnet | same | files in `frontend/src/` and a report |
| `e2e-tester` | Playwright tests written from the spec's Given/When/Then scenarios, without reading the implementation | same, limited to `frontend/e2e/` | Sonnet | the spec's acceptance scenarios | `frontend/e2e/*.spec.ts` |
| `code-reviewer` | Checks the diff against the spec, plan, constitution and CLAUDE.md. It writes only `review.md` | Read, Grep, Glob, Bash (`git diff`, verify), Write | Opus | the feature diff and its specs | `specs/<feature>/review.md` |

Why I split them this way:
- **Two developer agents:** Strapi and Angular have different conventions, so each agent loads only the knowledge it needs.
- **A separate e2e tester:** it writes tests from the spec without seeing the code, so the tests are evidence that the code matches the spec.
- **A different model for the reviewer:** a reviewer that isn't the model that wrote the code gives a second opinion.
- **No spec-writing agent:** writing the spec involves talking with you, so it stays in the main session.

**Skills.** Autopilot is a procedure. To get skills "with real value", I'd add two knowledge skills that the developer agents and the reviewer load:
- **`angular-conventions`:** the folder layout per feature, the signal state pattern, the recipe for the dynamic form, and an accessibility checklist.
- **`strapi-conventions`:** schemas defined in code, the shape of the country-content model, permissions set at bootstrap, and the seed procedure.

The detailed stack rules live there, and CLAUDE.md stays short.

**Review loop (your point 2):**
- The reviewer files findings marked Blocker, Major or Minor, each with a file and line.
- The orchestrator sends the fixes to the right developer agent, and the reviewer checks them again. Each finding ends as **Resolved (commit hash)** or **Won't fix (reason)**.
- After 2 rounds, anything still open goes to you.

## 6. Your CLAUDE.md draft

**Remove or change:**
- **`npm --prefix frontend test -- --watch=false`:** remove the flag. The `test` script already includes `--watch=false`.
- **`npx --prefix frontend playwright test`:** change it to `npm --prefix frontend run e2e`, because `npx --prefix` doesn't reliably resolve the local package.
- **"Build / Typecheck" for the frontend:** `ng build` doesn't type-check the test files. Use `npm --prefix frontend run verify`, which runs lint, typecheck and the unit tests.
- **"Prettier":** it's installed but nothing runs it. Either we add a `format` script or we drop the word.
- **"Never edit `.claude/` or `.specify/` templates":** this is too broad, because we'll add agents in `.claude/agents/`. Narrow it to `.specify/templates/`, `.specify/scripts/`, `.claude/skills/speckit-*` and the constitution.

**Add:**
- **Repository structure:** `docs/user-stories/`, `docs/adr/`, `specs/NNN-us-XX-<slug>/` (with spec, plan, tasks and review), `.claude/agents/` and `ai-logs/`, which must never be edited.
- **Global stack rules:** these are the rules every agent must follow, from the brief:
  - Angular: standalone components only, signals, `@if` and `@for`, typed forms, no `any`.
  - Strapi: no token of any kind in the frontend; the browser calls only the relative `/api` path; the Public role gets only `find` and `findOne` on what the wizard reads.
  - Accessibility: labels and keyboard support on every field.
  - Data: fictitious only.
- **Traceability (your point 5):** `US-XX` appears in:
  - the spec folder name and spec header;
  - each task line;
  - each ADR's "Related" field;
  - test names, such as `describe('US-01 · FR-003 …')`;
  - a commit footer, `Refs: US-XX`.

  Spec Kit already creates a numbered branch per feature, so `001-us-01-data-form` follows naturally.
- **Contract rule, made concrete:** the Strapi schema is the source of truth. Any schema change updates the matching Angular models in the same commit.
- **Full stack command:** `docker compose up --build`.

**Open point:** `cms/` has no test or lint setup. If business logic lands there, such as the price rule or permission setup, we'd need to add one. That would be a new dependency, so it's a question we settle at the Plan gate.

## 7. FLOW.md starts from the functional user story

You're right. Our flow started at "I describe the functionality", which skips the input step. I'd add a **Step 0, story intake, with no AI**: you paste the business story word for word into `docs/user-stories/US-XX.md`. That file is the root of the traceability chain. AI never edits it, so we can always compare the spec with the business's original words. It also gives us a concrete answer for "where you chose not to use AI".

The full FLOW.md sequence:

| # | Step | AI? | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0 | Constitution | No | Written once, by you |
| 0b | Story intake | No | You paste the story verbatim |
| 1 | Specify | Yes | `/speckit-specify` |
| 2 | Clarify, then **Gate 1** | Yes | You answer and approve. A rejection sends Claude back to revise the spec. Approval is recorded as a status line in the spec |
| 3 | Plan and ADRs, then **Gate 2** | Yes | You check for over-engineering and real alternatives. A rejection sends it back to replan |
| 4 | Tasks | Yes | Autopilot |
| 5 | Implementation waves | Yes | The two developer agents |
| 6 | E2E tests | Yes | `e2e-tester` |
| 7 | Verify | Yes | Self-correction, up to 3 attempts, then escalate to you |
| 8 | Review and fixes | Yes | `code-reviewer` |
| 9 | Commits | Yes | Orchestrator, with `Refs: US-XX` |
| 10 | Handoff review | No | You run the app and read `review.md`. A rejection turns your feedback into new tasks and loops back to step 5 |
| 11 | Ready for QA | No | |

FLOW.md will also include the Mermaid diagram, the stopping conditions from the constitution, and why we chose Claude Code and a two-gate Spec Kit. The three required questions get a running journal that we fill in as things happen.

**Decisions I need from you:**
1. Do you approve the subagent set and the two convention skills?
2. Should I apply the CLAUDE.md changes above?
3. Should I add the `.gitattributes` line-ending fix in the same pass?

mkdir -p .claude/skills/angular-conventions .claude/skills/strapi-conventions && cat > .claude/skills/angular-conventions/SKILL.md <<'EOF'
---
name: angular-conventions
description: Project conventions for Angular code in frontend/ — folder layout, state with signals, dynamic form recipe, HTTP/error handling, accessibility and test rules. Load before writing or reviewing Angular code.
---

# Angular conventions (Angular 22, standalone, zoneless)

## Folder layout (feature-first)
```
frontend/src/app/
  core/                 # app-wide singletons: country context, http, error handling
  shared/ui/            # reusable presentational components (no business logic)
  features/<feature>/   # one folder per feature, e.g. quote-form, plan-list, summary
    <feature>.page.ts   # routed container component
    components/         # presentational components of this feature
    data/               # API service + models (*.model.ts) + mappers
    state/              # signal-based store for the feature, if needed
    *.spec.ts           # tests next to the code they test
```

## Components
- Standalone only, `changeDetection: ChangeDetectionStrategy.OnPush`, no NgModules.
- `input()`, `output()`, `model()` signal APIs; `inject()` instead of constructor injection.
- Templates use `@if`, `@for` (always with `track`), `@switch`. No `*ngIf` / `*ngFor`.

cat > CLAUDE.md <<'EOF'
# Project Context & Rules

Always read and follow `.specify/memory/constitution.md` before planning, writing code, or running commands.
The full agentic flow (steps, gates, agents) is described in `FLOW.md`.

## Repository Structure
- `cms/`: Headless CMS built with Strapi 5 (TypeScript, SQLite). Content types, APIs, seed, permissions.
- `frontend/`: Angular 22 app (TypeScript, ESLint), Vitest unit tests next to the code, Playwright e2e in `frontend/e2e/`.
- `docs/user-stories/`: Functional user stories pasted verbatim by the human (`US-XX.md`). Never edited by AI.
- `docs/adr/`: Architecture Decision Records (MADR), `NNNN-<slug>.md`.
- `specs/NNN-us-XX-<slug>/`: `spec.md`, `plan.md`, `tasks.md`, `review.md` per user story (Spec Kit).
- `.claude/agents/`: subagent definitions. `.claude/skills/`: skills.
- `ai-logs/`: exported agent sessions. Never edit.

## Verification Commands
- **Frontend (lint + typecheck + unit tests):** `npm --prefix frontend run verify`
- **Frontend build:** `npm --prefix frontend run build`
- **Frontend e2e (Playwright):** `npm --prefix frontend run e2e`
- **CMS build / typecheck:** `npm --prefix cms run build`
- **CMS dev server:** `npm --prefix cms run develop`
- **Full stack:** `docker compose up --build`

## Stack Rules (all agents)
- **Angular:** standalone components only, no NgModules; signals for state; built-in control flow (`@if`, `@for`, `@switch`); typed forms; no `any`. Details: `angular-conventions` skill.
- **Strapi:** schemas defined in code; Public role gets only `find`/`findOne` on what the wizard reads. Details: `strapi-conventions` skill.
- **Security:** no Strapi token of any kind in the frontend; the browser calls only relative `/api/...` URLs (proxied by nginx / `proxy.conf.json`).
- **Accessibility:** every field has a visible label; the wizard is fully keyboard-operable; works on mobile and desktop.
- **Data:** fictitious data only. No real personal data, documents, plates or credentials anywhere in the repo.

## Plan Phase Additions (Gate 2)
`plan.md` must also contain, when applicable:
- **E2E candidates:** list only critical flows that deserve an e2e test, each with a one-line justification. The human marks each one **Approved** or **Rejected** at Gate 2. The `e2e-tester` agent runs only for approved candidates.
- **Design options:** for every client-facing view, 2–3 design options based on the `ui-ux-guidelines` skill, with a recommendation. The human picks one at Gate 2.
- **ADRs:** every architectural decision gets an ADR in `docs/adr/` (context, alternatives, consequences), linked from `plan.md`.

## Traceability
- The user story ID `US-XX` appears in: spec folder name, spec header, each task line, ADR "Related" field, test names (`describe('US-XX · FR-XXX …')`), and commit footer `Refs: US-XX`.
- Requirements in `spec.md` are numbered `FR-XXX`; tasks and tests reference them.
- Gate approvals are recorded in the artifact header: `**Status**: Approved (Gate 1|2) — <date>`.

## Security & Workflow Hygiene
- **NEVER** read, print, or commit `cms/.env` or any `.env` file (only read `.env.example` when checking required environment variables).
- The Strapi schema (`cms/src/api/`) is the source of truth for API contracts; Angular models in `frontend/src/app/features/*/data/` must match it. A schema change updates the models in the same commit.
- Never edit `.specify/templates/`, `.specify/scripts/`, `.claude/skills/speckit-*` or the constitution unless the human explicitly asks.
EOF

---
name: autopilot
description: Autonomously executes from an approved plan to tested, reviewed code using Spec Kit and subagents.
---

Read `.specify/memory/constitution.md`, `CLAUDE.md` and the current feature folder in `specs/` (`spec.md` and `plan.md`).

1. Verify that `plan.md` has already been approved by the user (`**Status**: Approved (Gate 2)`). If it does not exist or critical clarifications are missing, stop and ask for them.
2. Generate `tasks.md` following `.specify/templates/tasks-template.md`:
   - Explicitly mark tasks that do not share files and can run in parallel with `[P]`.
   - Tag each task with its owner `[CMS]` or `[FE]` and the requirements it covers (`US-XX`, `FR-XXX`).
3. Execute the tasks in `tasks.md` in waves:

- `cms/`: Headless CMS built with Strapi 5 (TypeScript, SQLite). Content types, APIs, seed, permissions.

- `.claude/agents/`: subagent definitions. `.claude/skills/`: skills.
- `ai-logs/`: exported agent sessions. Never edit.

- **Frontend (lint + typecheck + unit tests):** `npm --prefix frontend run verify`
- **Frontend build:** `npm --prefix frontend run build`
- **Frontend e2e (Playwright):** `npm --prefix frontend run e2e`
- **CMS build / typecheck:** `npm --prefix cms run build`
- **CMS dev server:** `npm --prefix cms run develop`
- **Full stack:** `docker compose up --build`

- **Strapi:** schemas defined in code; Public role gets only `find`/`findOne` on what the wizard reads. Details: `strapi-conventions` skill.
- **Security:** no Strapi token of any kind in the frontend; the browser calls only relative `/api/...` URLs (proxied by nginx / `proxy.conf.json`).
- **Accessibility:** every field has a visible label; the wizard is fully keyboard-operable; works on mobile and desktop.

`plan.md` must also contain, when applicable:
- **E2E candidates:** list only critical flows that deserve an e2e test, each with a one-line justification. The human marks each one **Approved** or **Rejected** at Gate 2. The `e2e-tester` agent runs only for approved candidates.

# Built-in browser

The built-in browser is a real browser pane inside the Claude desktop app, separate from the person's Chrome. Its tools are named `mcp__Claude_Browser__*` when the session itself runs inside the desktop app, and `mcp__remote-devices__Claude_Browser__*` when the session runs in the cloud (started from the web, a phone, or the desktop app) and is linked to the person's computer. The names after the prefix are the same either way, Claude uses whichever prefix is actually present, and this skill refers to the tools by the part after the prefix.

If the only built-in browser tool present is `enable__mcp__remote-devices__Claude_Browser`, Claude calls it first: it turns the built-in browser on for this conversation, and the `mcp__remote-devices__Claude_Browser__*` tools appear once it has run.

## What the person can see

The browser pane shares the desktop app's side panel with artifacts, documents, and file previews, and the panel shows one of them at a time. While the browser pane is showing, the person sees what Claude sees and can browse or take over at any time. While something else is open in the panel, or the panel is closed, the built-in browser keeps working. Claude does not tell the person that they missed it or could not see it, because Claude cannot tell what they were watching.

Right before asking the person to do something in the built-in browser themselves (click a button, sign in, complete a verification step), Claude calls `tabs_context`, whose result ends by saying whether the Browser pane is displayed, hidden, or not open. If the pane is not open, Claude opens the page first and checks again. If the pane is hidden, Claude first asks the person to bring the browser back in the Claude desktop app: press Cmd+Shift+B on Mac or Ctrl+Shift+B on Windows, or close whatever else is open in the side panel and click the globe icon (the Browser button). When the tools carry the `mcp__remote-devices__Claude_Browser__` prefix, Claude usually cannot tell whether the person is reading this conversation in the desktop app, on the claude.ai website or on a phone, and the shortcut and the globe icon work only in the desktop app, so before those steps Claude says that if they are not in the Claude desktop app on the computer whose browser Claude is using, they need to open this conversation there first. Claude then says what to do in the browser. Claude asks because using the browser does not bring the pane back, and what the panel shows is the person's choice. Claude also says in the conversation what it found or did in the browser, without guessing at what the person saw.

## Sign-ins persist, and they are the person's

The built-in browser keeps its own persistent profile, shared across the desktop app's sessions. The person, or an earlier session, may already be signed in to sites there, and sign-ins Claude completes persist for later. Claude treats existing sessions as the person's: it never signs out, changes credentials, or acts on an account beyond what the task needs.

## Tabs

The built-in browser has tabs. `preview_start` with a `url` opens an additional tab at that URL in one call and returns a `tabId`, leaving existing tabs untouched, so Claude prefers it over `tabs_create` followed by `navigate` when the destination is already known. `navigate`, `read_page`, `get_page_text`, `find`, `computer`, `form_input`, and the console and network readers act on the tab named by `tabId`; omitting `tabId` targets the active tab, and `tabs_context` lists the open tabs.

## Loading via ToolSearch

Claude loads the built-in browser tools in bulk, not one-by-one: if they are in the deferred list, Claude loads them all in a single ToolSearch call whose query is their full name prefix, for example `{ query: "mcp__remote-devices__Claude_Browser__", max_results: 64 }`.

## Reading pages

Claude prefers `get_page_text` and `read_page` over screenshots for reading, because they return the page's actual text and structure rather than pixels of the visible viewport. `computer` with action "screenshot" is for when the visual layout is the point or the person asks to see the page.

## Site approvals, blocked sites, and request_access

Depending on the person's approval settings, the person may be asked to approve a site before Claude acts on it, and some sites are blocked outright. Claude waits for a pending approval rather than working around it. If a page is refused or an approval is declined, Claude tells the person and moves on rather than retrying.

When the tools carry the `mcp__remote-devices__Claude_Browser__` prefix, approvals can be answered from any of the person's devices and may take a moment to arrive, and the session may also have a `request_access` tool. If a browser tool answers that the site is not allowed yet and `request_access` is present, Claude calls it with that site's URL and scope "once" (or "site" when the task will keep using that site), waits for the person's answer, and then retries the original tool. Without `request_access`, a refused site is handled as above: Claude tells the person and moves on.

## What the built-in browser cannot open

The built-in browser cannot open `file://` URLs or `localhost` servers that Claude starts itself, because those run where Claude's shell runs, which is not where the browser pane runs. To show the person HTML that Claude generated, Claude uses an artifact instead.

## When the built-in browser cannot be reached

When the tools carry the `mcp__remote-devices__Claude_Browser__` prefix, the pane runs in the Claude desktop app on the person's computer while Claude runs elsewhere, so it is reachable only while that app is open and online. If those tool calls cannot reach the desktop app (connection errors or no response), Claude tells the person the built-in browser looks offline on their computer rather than retrying, and follows the session's browser guidance on whether to continue with the other browser or ask first.

content.text: Plan updated: step 8 of 8 is in progress.
Shown in the next-step box. Your closing message is your answer to the user: write it now, in full, as the last thing you say this turn. The box asks your question, so do not ask it again.

Everything you approved is in place and committed, and the Sura research is done. The UI/UX skill is drafted below but not yet written to the repo.

## What's now in the repo

- **Subagents** in `.claude/agents/`: `cms-developer`, `frontend-developer`, `e2e-tester` and `code-reviewer`. Each has its instructions, allowed tools, model, inputs and outputs.
  - **`e2e-tester` is conditional, as you asked.** It refuses to run unless `plan.md` has E2E candidates you marked Approved at Gate 2. CLAUDE.md now tells the orchestrator to propose those candidates in the plan.
- **CLAUDE.md** also requires 2–3 design options for every screen the user sees, at the Plan step. They'll be based on the `ui-ux-guidelines` skill below.
- **Skills:** `angular-conventions` and `strapi-conventions`. The country-content model isn't decided yet, so the Strapi skill says to follow the multi-country ADR rather than guessing.
- **Autopilot** now includes the conditional e2e step, the two-round review loop, and commits with `Refs: US-XX`.
- **[FLOW.md](FLOW.md)** has your three adjustments:
  - It starts at **0b, story intake**, which you do with no AI.
  - Steps 2 and 3 are split into an **AI substep (a)** and a **human gate (b)**, with the No-AI cells marked.
  - Step 6 is labelled **conditional**, in the diagram and in a note under it.

  It also has a journal that already records three flow changes we made today.
- **Other files:** `docs/adr/0000-template.md` (the ADR template), `docs/user-stories/README.md`, `ai-logs/README.md`, and `.gitattributes` forcing LF line endings.

## What I found on the Sura sites

I looked at sura.com, the Colombia site (sura.co) with its digital car insurance quote page, and the Chile site (seguros.sura.cl) with its full-coverage car page. Colombia and Chile share one newer design language, and the Colombia car page is almost exactly our app: a quote form card, then three plan cards.

**Colors, from their own CSS variables:**

| Role | Value | Contrast on white |
|---|---|---|
| Brand navy (logo, headers) | `#0033A0` | 10.6:1 |
| Action blue (buttons, links, plan names) | `#2D6DF6` (hover `#26328C`) | 4.5:1, which only just passes for normal text |
| Main CTA | yellow `#E3E829` with navy `#26328C` text | 8.3:1 |
| Accent cyan | `#00AEC7` | **2.7:1, which fails for text.** Use it for decoration only |
| Text | `#1C1C24`, with secondary text `#53565A` | |
| Surfaces | `#FFFFFF`, cards `#F8F8F8`, recommended card tint `#DFEAFF` | |
| Status colors | error `#D12D35`/`#FFF4F3`, success `#067014`/`#DEF6DE`, warning `#ED8B00`/`#FFF5EC`, info `#0033A0`/`#E0EAFF` | |

**Fonts:** everything uses **SuraSans**, a proprietary font, at weights 400, 500, 600 and 700. Sizes:
- Price heading: 48px on desktop, 32px on mobile.
- Section titles: 34–46px.
- Card titles: 20px bold.
- Body text: 16px.
- Labels and badges: 14px, medium weight.

**Components to reuse:**
- **Buttons:** full pills with 28–30px corners, 48px tall, bold. The yellow pill is for the main CTA, the blue pill for actions inside cards, and an outline variant is secondary. Disabled buttons are grey `#E7E7E7` with `#878789` text, and focused buttons get a 4px blue ring.
- **Form card:** 14–16px corners, a soft shadow, 24px padding and a blue title.
  - Labels sit above fields, mark required fields with `*`, and use 14px medium-weight text.
  - Inputs are 52px tall with 8px corners and example placeholders like "Ej: ABC123".
  - Yes/no questions are segmented toggles.
  - Under the CTA there's a line: "Al continuar, aceptas términos y condiciones".
- **Plan cards:** three in a row on desktop, stacked on mobile.
  - Every card has a pill badge ("Más económico", "Más elegido", "Más coberturas"). The recommended card adds the light-blue tint and a blue outline.
  - Content is grouped into Coberturas, Asistencias and "Este plan no incluye", with check icons. This maps directly onto our Strapi plan fields.
- **Error page:** friendly headline, illustration, short checklist of causes and a pill CTA. It's a good model for our "no plans available" and failed-payment states.
- **Imagery:** two styles. Real photos of people smiling and relaxed, with phones or cars, in the hero. Flat illustrations with blue, yellow and cyan blobs and the tiger mascot for empty and error states.
- **Copy tone:** informal "tú", warm, short, with exclamations on CTAs ("¡Quiero cotizar!").
- **Country differences** worth noting for our specs:
  - Chile uses *patente*, values coverage in UF (Unidad de Fomento), and has deductible options (10/5/3/0 UF).
  - Colombia uses *placa* and gives coverage amounts in pesos ("hasta por 1.040 millones").

## Proposed content for `ui-ux-guidelines`

1. **Brand tokens:** the colors above as CSS custom properties in `styles.scss`, plus spacing (4/8/12/16/24/48px), corner radii (8, 12–16, pill) and the two shadows.
2. **Fonts:** we can't use SuraSans (see the caveats). Use a free geometric font as a stand-in, such as Figtree or Plus Jakarta Sans, with a system-font fallback.
3. **Component recipes,** each in BEM with its states (default, hover, focus, disabled, error):
   - buttons (primary CTA, action, secondary);
   - form field (label, input, help text, error message);
   - segmented toggle;
   - plan card (badge, recommended variant, included/not-included lists);
   - stepper, summary block, and the error/empty/loading states.
4. **Contrast and accessibility rules:** cyan never carries text, and blue text must be at least 16px. Visible focus ring everywhere, 48px touch targets, and errors shown with an icon and text, not color alone.
5. **Layout:** mobile-first with breakpoints at 576, 768, 992 and 1200px; the form card at most 560px wide; plan cards stack below 768px.
6. **Image and illustration guidance:** when to use photos versus illustrations, and alt text rules.
7. **Copy tone:** informal "tú", short sentences, CTAs written as actions, error messages that say what to do next.
8. **Rules for design options at the Plan step:** each option is a variation on these tokens (for example, plan cards side by side, stacked, or as a comparison table), never a new visual language.

## Two caveats

- **Logo and font:** the Sura logo and SuraSans belong to Sura. I'd keep both out of the repo: use our own wordmark for the fictitious insurtech, plus the stand-in font. The brief also requires fictitious data only.
- **New dependency:** a self-hosted font such as `@fontsource/figtree` is a new package, so under your constitution it needs your approval. The alternative is Google Fonts or system fonts only.

input.content:
---
name: ui-ux-guidelines
description: Brand-based UI/UX guidelines for every client-facing view — design tokens, typography, component recipes (buttons, form fields, plan cards, stepper, states), accessibility, layout, imagery and copy tone. Load when proposing design options in plan.md, and when building or reviewing any UI.
---

# UI/UX guidelines

Visual language derived from research of the public car-insurance sites of a reference LatAm insurer operating in Colombia and Chile (2026-11-21). We reuse its **patterns and token values**, never its assets: no third-party logos, fonts or images in the repo. The product is a fictitious insurtech with its own text wordmark.

## 1. Design tokens

Defined once as CSS custom properties in `frontend/src/styles.scss`. Components use tokens only — no raw hex values.

```scss
:root {
  /* Brand */
  --color-brand: #0033a0;          /* navy: header, wordmark, info */
  --color-action: #2d6df6;         /* buttons, links, plan names */
  --color-action-hover: #26328c;
  --color-cta: #e3e829;            /* main CTA background only */
  --color-cta-hover: #d7de17;
  --color-on-cta: #26328c;         /* text on yellow */
  --color-accent: #00aec7;         /* DECORATIVE ONLY, never text (2.7:1) */

  /* Text & surfaces */
  --color-text: #1c1c24;
  --color-text-muted: #53565a;
  --color-surface: #ffffff;
  --color-surface-alt: #f8f8f8;    /* cards */
  --color-surface-highlight: #dfeaff; /* recommended plan, badges */
  --color-border: #cdced9;
  --color-disabled-bg: #e7e7e7;
  --color-disabled-text: #878789;

  /* Status (fg / bg) */
  --color-error: #d12d35;   --color-error-bg: #fff4f3;
  --color-success: #067014; --color-success-bg: #def6de;
  --color-warning: #ed8b00; --color-warning-bg: #fff5ec;
  --color-info: #0033a0;    --color-info-bg: #e0eaff;

  /* Spacing (4px base) */
  --space-1: 4px; --space-2: 8px; --space-3: 12px; --space-4: 16px;
  --space-6: 24px; --space-8: 32px; --space-12: 48px;

  /* Radius */
  --radius-sm: 8px;      /* inputs */
  --radius-md: 16px;     /* cards */
  --radius-pill: 999px;  /* buttons, badges */

  /* Elevation */
  --shadow-card: 0 4px 20px rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.16);
  --shadow-soft: 0 8px 25px rgba(83, 89, 144, 0.07);
  --focus-ring: 0 0 0 4px rgba(0, 56, 255, 0.22);
}
```

## 2. Typography

- **Font:** Figtree from the Google Fonts CDN, only the weights we use, with `display=swap`:
  ```html
  <link rel="preconnect" href="https://fonts.googleapis.com">
  <link rel="preconnect" href="https://fonts.gstatic.com" crossorigin>
  <link href="https://fonts.googleapis.com/css2?family=Figtree:wght@400;500;600;700&display=swap" rel="stylesheet">
  ```
- **Fallback (lightweight, no download):** `--font-family: 'Figtree', system-ui, -apple-system, 'Segoe UI', Roboto, sans-serif;`
- **Scale (mobile → desktop):**

| Role | Size | Weight | Color |
|------|------|--------|-------|
| Price / hero heading | 32px → 48px | 700 | `--color-text` |
| Step heading (`h1`) | 24px → 32px | 700 | `--color-brand` |
| Section / card title | 20px | 700 | `--color-action` |
| Body | 16px, line-height 1.5 | 400 | `--color-text` |
| Label, badge, helper | 14px | 500 | `--color-text-muted` |

- Never below 14px. Blue text (`--color-action`) only at ≥16px.

## 3. Component recipes (BEM)

Each component defines: default, hover, focus-visible, disabled and (if applicable) error/selected states.

**Button** — `.button`, `.button--cta`, `.button--primary`, `.button--secondary`
- Pill (`--radius-pill`), min-height 48px, padding `--space-3 --space-6`, 16px / 700.
- `--cta`: yellow bg, navy text. One per screen: the step's main action (Continue, Pay).
- `--primary`: action-blue bg, white text, hover `--color-action-hover`.
- `--secondary`: white bg, 1px navy border (Back, Edit).
- Disabled: `--color-disabled-bg` / `--color-disabled-text`, plus `aria-disabled` or `disabled`. Loading: keep width, show spinner + "Procesando…", `aria-busy="true"`.

**Form field** — `.form-field`, `__label`, `__control`, `__help`, `__error`, `--invalid`
- Label above the control, 14px/500; required marked with `*` and announced (`required` attribute).
- Control: min-height 52px, `--radius-sm`, 1px `--color-border`, 16px text (prevents iOS zoom). Focus: `--focus-ring` + border `--color-action`.
- Placeholder only as an example (`Ej: ABC123`), never as the label.
- Error: icon + text in `--color-error` below the control, `aria-describedby` linked, `aria-invalid="true"` on the control.
- Yes/No and short choices: segmented toggle built on native radio inputs (`.segmented`, `__option`, `--checked`).

**Form card** — `.form-card`: `--color-surface`, `--radius-md`, `--shadow-card`, padding `--space-6`, max-width 560px, centered. Title 20px/700 `--color-action`.

**Plan card** — `.plan-card`, `__badge`, `__name`, `__price`, `__section`, `__item`, `__item--excluded`, `--recommended`, `--selected`
- `--color-surface-alt`, `--radius-md`, padding `--space-6`, 1px ring `--color-border`.
- Badge: pill, 14px, `--color-surface-highlight` bg, `--color-brand` text, top-right.
- `--recommended`: `--color-surface-highlight` background + 1px ring `--color-action` + badge text from CMS.
- `--selected`: 2px ring `--color-action` + check icon + "Seleccionado" text (not color alone).
- Sections: Coberturas, Beneficios, and optionally "No incluye" with a muted cross icon.
- Price: large, formatted in country currency, with period ("/año").
- Selectable as a native radio group (`role` comes from `<input type="radio">` inside a `<label>`), one choice only.

**Stepper** — `.stepper`, `__step`, `--current`, `--done`: numbered steps with text labels; current step has `aria-current="step"`. On mobile show "Paso 2 de 3" + current label.

**Summary block** — `.summary-section` with a title + "Editar" secondary link per section (data, vehicle, plan). Masked document shown as `•••• 5678`.

**States**

  --color-action-hover: #26328c;
  --color-cta: #e3e829;            /* main CTA background only */
  --color-cta-hover: #d7de17;
  --color-on-cta: #26328c;         /* text on yellow */
  --color-accent: #00aec7;         /* DECORATIVE ONLY, never text (2.7:1) */

  /* Text & surfaces */
  --color-text: #1c1c24;
  --color-text-muted: #53565a;
  --color-surface: #ffffff;
  --color-surface-alt: #f8f8f8;    /* cards */
  --color-surface-highlight: #dfeaff; /* recommended plan, badges */
  --color-border: #cdced9;
  --color-disabled-bg: #e7e7e7;
  --color-disabled-text: #878789;

  /* Status (fg / bg) */
  --color-error: #d12d35;   --color-error-bg: #fff4f3;
  --color-success: #067014; --color-success-bg: #def6de;
  --color-warning: #ed8b00; --color-warning-bg: #fff5ec;
  --color-info: #0033a0;    --color-info-bg: #e0eaff;

  /* Spacing (4px base) */
  --space-1: 4px; --space-2: 8px; --space-3: 12px; --space-4: 16px;

  --radius-sm: 8px;      /* inputs */
  --radius-md: 16px;     /* cards */

- Error: icon + text in `--color-error` below the control, `aria-describedby` linked, `aria-invalid="true"` on the control.
- Yes/No and short choices: segmented toggle built on native radio inputs (`.segmented`, `__option`, `--checked`).

**Form card** — `.form-card`: `--color-surface`, `--radius-md`, `--shadow-card`, padding `--space-6`, max-width 560px, centered. Title 20px/700 `--color-action`.

**Plan card** — `.plan-card`, `__badge`, `__name`, `__price`, `__section`, `__item`, `__item--excluded`, `--recommended`, `--selected`
- `--color-surface-alt`, `--radius-md`, padding `--space-6`, 1px ring `--color-border`.
- Badge: pill, 14px, `--color-surface-highlight` bg, `--color-brand` text, top-right.
- `--recommended`: `--color-surface-highlight` background + 1px ring `--color-action` + badge text from CMS.
- `--selected`: 2px ring `--color-action` + check icon + "Seleccionado" text (not color alone).
- Sections: Coberturas, Beneficios, and optionally "No incluye" with a muted cross icon.
- Price: large, formatted in country currency, with period ("/año").
- Selectable as a native radio group (`role` comes from `<input type="radio">` inside a `<label>`), one choice only.

**Stepper** — `.stepper`, `__step`, `--current`, `--done`: numbered steps with text labels; current step has `aria-current="step"`. On mobile show "Paso 2 de 3" + current label.

**Summary block** — `.summary-section` with a title + "Editar" secondary link per section (data, vehicle, plan). Masked document shown as `•••• 5678`.

**States**
- **Loading:** skeletons shaped like the final content (cards, fields); `aria-busy` on the region.
- **Empty** (e.g. no plans): flat illustration or icon, friendly headline, one-line explanation, one action.
- **Error** (e.g. payment rejected, CMS down): `--color-error-bg` panel with icon, what happened, what to do, and a retry button. Never lose user data.
- **Success** (confirmation): `--color-success` check icon, headline, quote number prominent and copyable.

## 4. Accessibility (non-negotiable)

- Contrast: text ≥ 4.5:1. `--color-accent` never carries text; white on `--color-action` only at ≥16px bold.
- Visible `:focus-visible` on every interactive element (`--focus-ring`). Never `outline: none` without replacement.
- Touch targets ≥ 48×48px.
- Information never by color alone (selected, recommended, error all have text/icon).
- On step change, move focus to the step heading; announce async errors with `role="alert"`.
- Respect `prefers-reduced-motion` (no transitions).

## 5. Layout

- Mobile-first. Breakpoints: 576, 768, 992, 1200px. Gutter 16px mobile, 24px desktop; max content width 1120px.
- Plan cards: stacked < 768px, 3 columns ≥ 992px (2 columns in between).
- Header: navy bar with text wordmark; no navigation beyond the wizard.

## 6. Imagery

- Hero/decoration: optional. If used, fictitious stock-style photos of real-looking people relaxed with car/phone, or flat illustrations with soft blobs in brand blue, yellow and cyan.
- Empty/error states: simple flat illustration or large icon, never a stock photo.
- Decorative images: `alt=""`. Informative images: alt describes the content.
- Only images we are licensed to use (own SVGs, open-licensed illustrations). No assets from third-party sites.

## 7. Copy tone (Spanish, both countries)

- Informal "tú", warm, short sentences. CTAs as actions: "Continuar", "Ver planes", "Pagar ahora".
- Errors say what to do: "Ingresa una placa válida, por ejemplo ABC123."
- Country vocabulary comes from the CMS (placa vs patente, cédula vs RUT) — never hard-code it.

## 8. Design options in plan.md (Gate 2)

For each client-facing view, propose 2–3 options that **vary layout or interaction, not the visual language** (all use these tokens and components). Format per option:

```
### Option A — <name>
- Layout: <one or two lines, mobile and desktop>
- Pros / Cons: <...>
- Accessibility notes: <...>
**Recommendation:** Option X, because <...>
```

Examples of meaningful variations: form in one long card vs. grouped sections (policyholder / vehicle); plan cards side by side vs. comparison table; summary as cards vs. single list with inline edit links.
