# Multi-country car insurance quote

A single Angular app that quotes car insurance in **Colombia** and **Chile**, with every form field and plan managed from **Strapi**, built through an agentic flow with Claude Code and Spec Kit.

- **How it was built (the agentic flow):** [FLOW.md](FLOW.md)
- **Architecture decisions:** [docs/adr/](docs/adr/)
- **Specs per user story:** [specs/](specs/)

> All data in this repository is fictitious. No real people, documents, plates, card data or credentials.

## Quick start

Requirements: Docker Desktop (with Docker Compose v2).

```bash
docker compose up --build
```

| URL | What |
|-----|------|
| http://localhost:4200/co/quote | App, Colombia |
| http://localhost:4200/cl/quote | App, Chile |
| http://localhost:1337/admin | Strapi admin panel |

Seed data for both countries is loaded on the first start. The Strapi admin user is created automatically on the first start with **dev-only** credentials (see [Strapi admin user](#strapi-admin-user)).

To stop: `docker compose down`. To also reset the database: `docker compose down -v`.

## Local development (without Docker)

Requirements: Node.js 22+ and npm.

```bash
npm --prefix cms ci
npm --prefix frontend ci
cp cms/.env.example cms/.env   # then replace the placeholder secrets

npm --prefix cms run develop   # Strapi on http://localhost:1337
npm --prefix frontend start    # Angular on http://localhost:4200 (proxies /api to Strapi)
```

## Tests and checks

| Command | What it runs |
|---------|--------------|
| `npm --prefix frontend run verify` | Lint + typecheck + unit tests (Vitest) |
| `npm --prefix frontend run e2e` | Playwright e2e; starts Strapi and Angular itself |
| `npm --prefix frontend run e2e:docker` | Playwright e2e against the running Docker stack |
| `npm --prefix cms run build` | Strapi build and typecheck |

## Repository structure

| Path | Content |
|------|---------|
| `frontend/` | Angular app (standalone components, signals, built-in control flow) |
| `cms/` | Strapi 5 project: content types, seed data, permissions |
| `docs/user-stories/` | Functional user stories, verbatim |
| `docs/adr/` | Architecture Decision Records |
| `specs/` | Spec, plan, tasks and review per user story |
| `.specify/` | Spec Kit: constitution, templates, scripts |
| `.claude/agents/`, `.claude/skills/` | Subagent and skill definitions |
| `.claude/settings.json` | Agent permissions (allowlist and hard limits) |
| `CLAUDE.md` | Global context file for all agents |
| `ai-logs/` | Unedited exports of the agent sessions |

## Strapi admin user

_To be completed with US-01: the admin user is created at bootstrap from environment variables with dev-only defaults, documented here._

## Security notes

- The browser never receives a Strapi token. It calls only relative `/api/...` URLs, proxied to Strapi by nginx (Docker) or the Angular dev server.
- The Strapi Public role can only `find` the content the wizard reads (see [ADR 0001](docs/adr/0001-multi-country-content-strategy.md)).
- The secrets in `docker-compose.yml` are dev-only placeholders. Override them with a root `.env` file for anything beyond local use.

## Known issues and notes

- **Google Fonts:** the Figtree font is loaded from the Google Fonts CDN, so each visitor's IP address is sent to Google. A self-hosted font would avoid it.
- **npm audit:** `npm audit` reports vulnerabilities in Strapi's transitive dependencies. They are not patched with `npm audit fix --force` because that would break Strapi's pinned versions.

## Requirements not met

_None so far. Any requirement left out will be listed here with the reason._

# Project Context & Rules

Always read and follow `.specify/memory/constitution.md` before planning, writing code, or running commands.
The full agentic flow (steps, gates, agents) is described in `FLOW.md`.

## Repository Structure
- `cms/`: Headless CMS built with Strapi 5 (TypeScript, SQLite). Content types, APIs, seed, permissions.
- `frontend/`: Angular 22 app (TypeScript, ESLint), Vitest unit tests next to the code, Playwright e2e in `frontend/e2e/`.
- `docs/user-stories/`: Functional user stories pasted verbatim by the human (`US-XX.md`). Never edited by AI.
- `docs/adr/`: Architecture Decision Records (MADR), `NNNN-<slug>.md`.
- `specs/NNN-us-XX-<slug>/`: `spec.md`, `plan.md`, `tasks.md`, `review.md` per user story (Spec Kit).
- `.claude/agents/`: subagent definitions. `.claude/skills/`: skills.
- `ai-logs/`: exported agent sessions. Never edit.

## Verification Commands
- **Frontend (lint + typecheck + unit tests):** `npm --prefix frontend run verify`
- **Frontend build:** `npm --prefix frontend run build`
- **Frontend e2e (Playwright):** `npm --prefix frontend run e2e`
- **CMS build / typecheck:** `npm --prefix cms run build`
- **CMS dev server:** `npm --prefix cms run develop`
- **Full stack:** `docker compose up --build`

## Stack Rules (all agents)
- **Angular:** standalone components only, no NgModules; signals for state; built-in control flow (`@if`, `@for`, `@switch`); typed forms; no `any`. Details: `angular-conventions` skill.
- **Strapi:** schemas defined in code; Public role gets only `find`/`findOne` on what the wizard reads. Details: `strapi-conventions` skill.
- **Security:** no Strapi token of any kind in the frontend; the browser calls only relative `/api/...` URLs (proxied by nginx / `proxy.conf.json`).
- **Accessibility:** every field has a visible label; the wizard is fully keyboard-operable; works on mobile and desktop.
- **Data:** fictitious data only. No real personal data, documents, plates or credentials anywhere in the repo.

## Plan Phase Additions (Gate 2)
`plan.md` must also contain, when applicable:
- **E2E candidates:** list only critical flows that deserve an e2e test, each with a one-line justification. The human marks each one **Approved** or **Rejected** at Gate 2. The `e2e-tester` agent runs only for approved candidates.
- **Design options:** for every client-facing view, 2–3 design options based on the `ui-ux-guidelines` skill, with a recommendation. The human picks one at Gate 2.
- **ADRs:** every architectural decision gets an ADR in `docs/adr/` (context, alternatives, consequences), linked from `plan.md`.
- **Revisions:** when the human rejects or corrects the plan at Gate 2, append an entry to a `## Revisions` section at the end of `plan.md`: date, what the human asked to change, and what changed. Never delete entries.

## Traceability
- The user story ID `US-XX` appears in: spec folder name, spec header, each task line, ADR "Related" field, test names (`describe('US-XX · FR-XXX …')`), and commit footer `Refs: US-XX`.
- Requirements in `spec.md` are numbered `FR-XXX`; tasks and tests reference them.
- Gate approvals are recorded in the artifact header: `**Status**: Approved (Gate 1|2) — <date>`. Gate 3 is recorded as the last line of `review.md`: `Gate 3: Approved — <date>`.
- Human corrections: Gate 1 in `spec.md` › Clarifications, Gate 2 in `plan.md` › Revisions, Gate 3 as new tasks in `tasks.md`.

## Security & Workflow Hygiene
- **NEVER** read, print, or commit `cms/.env` or any `.env` file (only read `.env.example` when checking required environment variables).
- The Strapi schema (`cms/src/api/`) is the source of truth for API contracts; Angular models in `frontend/src/app/features/*/data/` must match it. A schema change updates the models in the same commit.
- Never edit `.specify/templates/`, `.specify/scripts/`, `.claude/skills/speckit-*` or the constitution unless the human explicitly asks.

---
name: autopilot
description: Autonomously executes from an approved plan to tested, reviewed code using Spec Kit and subagents.
---

Read `.specify/memory/constitution.md`, `CLAUDE.md` and the current feature folder in `specs/` (`spec.md` and `plan.md`).

1. Verify that `plan.md` has already been approved by the user (`**Status**: Approved (Gate 2)`). If it does not exist or critical clarifications are missing, stop and ask for them.
2. Generate `tasks.md` following `.specify/templates/tasks-template.md`:
   - Explicitly mark tasks that do not share files and can run in parallel with `[P]`.
   - Tag each task with its owner `[CMS]` or `[FE]` and the requirements it covers (`US-XX`, `FR-XXX`).
3. Execute the tasks in `tasks.md` in waves:
   - Spawn subagents in parallel for `[P]` task groups: `cms-developer` for `[CMS]`, `frontend-developer` for `[FE]`.

# Project Context & Rules

Always read and follow `.specify/memory/constitution.md` before planning, writing code, or running commands.
The full agentic flow (steps, gates, agents) is described in `FLOW.md`.

## Repository Structure
- `cms/`: Headless CMS built with Strapi 5 (TypeScript, SQLite). Content types, APIs, seed, permissions.
- `frontend/`: Angular 22 app (TypeScript, ESLint), Vitest unit tests next to the code, Playwright e2e in `frontend/e2e/`.
- `docs/user-stories/`: Functional user stories pasted verbatim by the human (`US-XX.md`). Never edited by AI.
- `docs/adr/`: Architecture Decision Records (MADR), `NNNN-<slug>.md`.
- `specs/NNN-us-XX-<slug>/`: `spec.md`, `plan.md`, `tasks.md`, `review.md` per user story (Spec Kit).
- `.claude/agents/`: subagent definitions. `.claude/skills/`: skills.
- `ai-logs/`: exported agent sessions. Never edit.

## Verification Commands
- **Frontend (lint + typecheck + unit tests):** `npm --prefix frontend run verify`
- **Frontend build:** `npm --prefix frontend run build`
- **Frontend e2e (Playwright):** `npm --prefix frontend run e2e`
- **CMS build / typecheck:** `npm --prefix cms run build`
- **CMS dev server:** `npm --prefix cms run develop`
- **Full stack:** `docker compose up --build`

## Stack Rules (all agents)
- **Angular:** standalone components only, no NgModules; signals for state; built-in control flow (`@if`, `@for`, `@switch`); typed forms; no `any`. Details: `angular-conventions` skill.
- **Strapi:** schemas defined in code; Public role gets only `find`/`findOne` on what the wizard reads. Details: `strapi-conventions` skill.
- **Security:** no Strapi token of any kind in the frontend; the browser calls only relative `/api/...` URLs (proxied by nginx / `proxy.conf.json`).
- **Accessibility:** every field has a visible label; the wizard is fully keyboard-operable; works on mobile and desktop.
- **Data:** fictitious data only. No real personal data, documents, plates or credentials anywhere in the repo.

## Plan Phase Additions (Gate 2)
`plan.md` must also contain, when applicable:
- **E2E candidates:** list only critical flows that deserve an e2e test, each with a one-line justification. The human marks each one **Approved** or **Rejected** at Gate 2. The `e2e-tester` agent runs only for approved candidates.
- **Design options:** for every client-facing view, 2–3 design options based on the `ui-ux-guidelines` skill, with a recommendation. The human picks one at Gate 2.
- **ADRs:** every architectural decision gets an ADR in `docs/adr/` (context, alternatives, consequences), linked from `plan.md`.
- **Revisions:** when the human rejects or corrects the plan at Gate 2, append an entry to a `## Revisions` section at the end of `plan.md`: date, what the human asked to change, and what changed. Never delete entries.

## Traceability
- The user story ID `US-XX` appears in: spec folder name, spec header, each task line, ADR "Related" field, test names (`describe('US-XX · FR-XXX …')`), and commit footer `Refs: US-XX`.
- Requirements in `spec.md` are numbered `FR-XXX`; tasks and tests reference them.
- Gate approvals are recorded in the artifact header: `**Status**: Approved (Gate 1|2) — <date>`. Gate 3 is recorded as the last line of `review.md`: `Gate 3: Approved — <date>`.
- Human corrections: Gate 1 in `spec.md` › Clarifications, Gate 2 in `plan.md` › Revisions, Gate 3 as new tasks in `tasks.md`.

## Security & Workflow Hygiene
- **NEVER** read, print, or commit `cms/.env` or any `.env` file (only read `.env.example` when checking required environment variables).
- The Strapi schema (`cms/src/api/`) is the source of truth for API contracts; Angular models in `frontend/src/app/features/*/data/` must match it. A schema change updates the models in the same commit.
- Never edit `.specify/templates/`, `.specify/scripts/`, `.claude/skills/speckit-*` or the constitution unless the human explicitly asks.

1	# 0002 — Agentic workflow: Spec Kit and 3 human gates
2	
3	- **Status:** Accepted
4	- **Date:** 2026-11-22
5	- **Related:** `FLOW.md`, `.specify/memory/constitution.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, all user stories
6	
7	## Context and problem
8	
9	The increment must go from a functional user story to QA-ready code through a system of AI agents, with people stepping in at points we define. The flow has to be explicit, justified, traceable and repeatable, and it has to stay as frictionless as possible: every human checkpoint costs time, but every missing one risks the agent inventing scope or over-engineering.
10	
11	So we need to decide:
12	
13	1. Which framework drives the flow from story to code.
14	2. Where the human steps in, and how much autonomy the agents get in between.
15	
16	## Decision drivers
17	
18	- Traceability from user story to QA.
19	- A single, approved source of truth that automatic checks can compare against.
20	- Detect gaps in the user story before building.
21	- Repeatable: the same flow every time.
22	- Low friction: as few human stops as possible, placed where they add the most value.
23	
24	## Decision
25	
26	**Spec Kit and 3 human gates**, running in Claude Code:

# 0002 — Agentic workflow: Spec Kit and 3 human gates

- **Status:** Accepted
- **Date:** 2026-11-22
- **Related:** `FLOW.md`, `.specify/memory/constitution.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, all user stories

## Context and problem

The increment must go from a functional user story to QA-ready code through a system of AI agents, with people stepping in at points we define. The flow has to be explicit, justified, traceable and repeatable, and it has to stay as frictionless as possible: every human checkpoint costs time, but every missing one risks the agent inventing scope or over-engineering.

So we need to decide:

1. Which framework drives the flow from story to code.
2. Where the human steps in, and how much autonomy the agents get in between.

## Decision drivers

- Traceability from user story to QA.
- A single, approved source of truth that automatic checks can compare against.
- Detect gaps in the user story before building.
- Repeatable: the same flow every time.
- Low friction: as few human stops as possible, placed where they add the most value.

## Decision

**Spec Kit and 3 human gates**, running in Claude Code:

- **Gate 1 — Spec** (after specify + clarify).
- **Gate 2 — Plan** (plan, ADRs, design option, E2E candidates).
- **Gate 3 — Handoff review** (before QA).

Between Gate 2 and Gate 3 the agents run on autopilot (tasks → implementation → verify → conditional E2E → review → commit), bounded by the stop conditions of the constitution.

### Why this one?

- **Traceable:** Spec Kit offers traceability by using git (a branch and a numbered spec folder per feature), which is good to get the whole path from user story to QA.
- **Spec as source:** this gives a valid and approved point of comparison for the different automatic checks within the flow.
- **Gap detection:** the built-in clarify skill detects gaps in the user story, which saves effort before building.
- **Global context:** the constitution.md serves as global project context, where we set limits and expected behaviors for agents.
- **Repeatable process:** every time we run the flow it is still the same, because of Spec Kit capabilities and default behavior.

### Why this human gate design?

- **Gates live where they contribute the most:** Gate 1 avoids a typical AI error: inventing scope or writing extra criteria. Gate 2 avoids another typical mistake: overdesign or overengineering. An error detected in the spec phase costs minutes, but in the handoff phase it can cost a new wave of implementation.
- **Every gate has its own criteria and a clear rejection path.**
- **Human revisions are logged:** Gate 1 corrections are saved into the spec's Clarifications, and Gate 2 corrections into the plan's Revisions.
- **Agent autonomy after approvals.**
- **The reviewer agent uses a different model**, which reduces blind spots.
- **Every agent has its own responsibilities, tools and skills.**
- **Conditional E2E, approved by the human.**

## Considered options

1. **Spec Kit with 3 human gates** (chosen).
2. **Spec Kit as-is, with a human review after every phase** (specify, clarify, plan, tasks, implement): maximum control, but the human stops the flow 5+ times per story. Not taken: too much friction, and reviewing `tasks.md` adds little over reviewing `plan.md`.
3. **Fully autonomous flow, no human gates:** fastest. Not taken: nobody would catch invented scope or over-engineering until QA, which is the most expensive point to find them.
4. **Our own SDD variant without a framework:** total freedom over templates and steps. Not taken: we would have to build and maintain what Spec Kit already gives (templates, numbered features, clarify), and the result would be less repeatable.
5. **Kiro (spec-driven IDE):** specs built into the tool. Not taken: it ties the flow to one IDE, and its subagents, skills and context file are less portable than Claude Code's versioned Markdown files.

## Consequences

- **Partial independence of the reviewer agent:** it belongs to the same family of models, so some blind spots are shared.
- **Heavy for small stories:** for a small user story the full flow can be heavy and expensive.
- **The human can become the bottleneck:** no story goes ahead without passing Gates 1 and 2.
- **Built for one developer:** this setup was designed for a solo developer working with an agent, not for a team.
- **No human in the loop from step 4 to step 9:** quality there depends on the reviewer agent and the automatic checks.

# 0001 — Multi-country content strategy (Strapi + Angular)

- **Status:** Proposed
- **Date:** 2026-11-21
- **Related:** US-00, US-01, US-02, US-03

### Decision

How does Angular know which country to render? Let's take the **path prefix** approach for its simplicity, e.g. `/co/quote` and `/cl/quote`. The path must always have the prefix.

- The prefix is the country `code` in lower case (`/co` ↔ `CO`).
- `/` is the **country selection screen** (US-00): it lists the countries returned by `GET /api/countries`, with the last country the user was visiting (saved in `sessionStorage`) preselected, if it is still active and available. No country code is hardcoded.
- Any unknown or unpublished prefix (e.g. `/pe/quote`) **redirects** to `/`.

### Advantages

- **Scalability:** a resolver or guard checks the code against `GET /api/countries`, not against an enum in code.
- **Separation of domains:** a `CountryContext` with a signal can feed each country separately, loading fields, plans, currency and the unique persistent key per country in `sessionStorage`.
- **Easy e2e per country:** just open each prefix.
- **Close to a production-ready solution:** in production, subdomains could be better and preferable, and they could be implemented without changing the current approach much.

### Tradeoff

- Changing the country in the middle of the wizard restarts it.
- A mistyped country in the URL sends the user to the selection screen instead of showing an error. Acceptable because the user picks the country again in one click.

## Considered options (not taken)

### i18n in Strapi with a locale per country

# Multi-country car insurance quote

A single Angular app that quotes car insurance in **Colombia** and **Chile**, with every form field and plan managed from **Strapi**, built through an agentic flow with Claude Code and Spec Kit.

- **How it was built (the agentic flow):** [FLOW.md](FLOW.md)
- **Architecture decisions:** [docs/adr/](docs/adr/)
- **Specs per user story:** [specs/](specs/)

> **Status:** project setup complete; the wizard, seed data and admin bootstrap are built story by story (US-01 → US-03). Sections marked _To be completed_ are filled as each story lands.

> All data in this repository is fictitious. No real people, documents, plates, card data or credentials.

## Quick start

Requirements: Docker Desktop (with Docker Compose v2).

```bash
docker compose up --build
```

| URL | What |
|-----|------|
| http://localhost:4200/co/quote | App, Colombia |
| http://localhost:4200/cl/quote | App, Chile |
| http://localhost:1337/admin | Strapi admin panel |

Seed data for both countries is loaded on the first start. The Strapi admin user is created automatically on the first start with **dev-only** credentials (see [Strapi admin user](#strapi-admin-user)).

To stop: `docker compose down`. To also reset the database: `docker compose down -v`.

## Local development (without Docker)

Requirements: Node.js 22+ and npm.

```bash
npm --prefix cms ci
npm --prefix frontend ci
cp cms/.env.example cms/.env   # then replace the placeholder secrets

npm --prefix cms run develop   # Strapi on http://localhost:1337
npm --prefix frontend start    # Angular on http://localhost:4200 (proxies /api to Strapi)
```

## Tests and checks

| Command | What it runs |
|---------|--------------|
| `npm --prefix frontend run verify` | Lint + typecheck + unit tests (Vitest) |
| `npm --prefix frontend run e2e` | Playwright e2e; starts Strapi and Angular itself |
| `npm --prefix frontend run e2e:docker` | Playwright e2e against the running Docker stack |
| `npm --prefix cms run build` | Strapi build and typecheck |

## Repository structure

| Path | Content |
|------|---------|
| `frontend/` | Angular app (standalone components, signals, built-in control flow) |
| `cms/` | Strapi 5 project: content types, seed data, permissions |
| `docs/user-stories/` | Functional user stories, verbatim |
| `docs/adr/` | Architecture Decision Records |
| `specs/` | Spec, plan, tasks and review per user story |
| `.specify/` | Spec Kit: constitution, templates, scripts |
| `.claude/agents/`, `.claude/skills/` | Subagent and skill definitions |
| `.claude/settings.json` | Agent permissions (allowlist and hard limits) |
| `CLAUDE.md` | Global context file for all agents |
| `ai-logs/` | Unedited exports of the agent sessions |

## Strapi admin user

_To be completed with US-01: the admin user is created at bootstrap from environment variables with dev-only defaults, documented here._

## Security notes

- The browser never receives a Strapi token. It calls only relative `/api/...` URLs, proxied to Strapi by nginx (Docker) or the Angular dev server.
- The Strapi Public role can only `find` the content the wizard reads (see [ADR 0001](docs/adr/0001-multi-country-content-strategy.md)).
- The secrets in `docker-compose.yml` are dev-only placeholders. Override them with a root `.env` file for anything beyond local use.

## Known issues and notes

- **Google Fonts:** the Figtree font is loaded from the Google Fonts CDN, so each visitor's IP address is sent to Google. A self-hosted font would avoid it.
- **npm audit:** `npm audit` reports vulnerabilities in Strapi's transitive dependencies. They are not patched with `npm audit fix --force` because that would break Strapi's pinned versions.

## Requirements not met

_None so far. Any requirement left out will be listed here with the reason._

One correction to your premise: between steps 4 and 8 there already was an automatic check, verify (step 7). But verify only tests the code. It doesn't check whether the tasks cover the spec, so your point stands: a missing requirement would only show up in review, after the code is written.

- **The autopilot runs Spec Kit's analyze step and handles its results itself.** The analyze skill is strictly read-only and would normally ask a person before fixing anything, so the autopilot adds these rules:
  - It saves each run's report to `specs/<feature>/analysis.md`.
  - **Gaps in `tasks.md`**, such as a requirement with no tasks or a task with no requirement, are fixed automatically and analyze runs again, up to 3 times.
  - **A finding that needs a change to `spec.md` or `plan.md` stops and goes to you.** Those were approved at Gates 1 and 2, and changing them silently would bypass the gates. This is the only case where the check stops.
  - Code is written only once the last run has no CRITICAL or HIGH findings.
- **ADR 0002** is marked "amended", with the reason, and its "no human from step 4 to 9" consequence now lists all the automatic checks.
- **CLAUDE.md** now lists `analysis.md` in each spec folder.

## US-00 – Country selection

### Story

As a person interested in insuring my car, I want to choose the country where I want
to buy the insurance, so that the form, plans, prices and terms I see apply to my country.

### Context

The same application sells car insurance in Colombia and Chile. Everything the person
sees in the following steps (form fields, plans, currency, terms and conditions) depends
on the country, so the country must be known before the wizard starts. The business team
wants to manage the available countries from Strapi, including their name and flag or
icon, so that a new country can be offered without changing code.

### Business rules

- The available countries are configured in Strapi with: name, code, icon, order and
  active status.
- Only published and active countries are shown, in the configured order.
- Only one country can be selected.
- The selected country is reflected in the address, so a shared link opens the
  application directly in that country, without going through the selection screen.
- If the address contains a country that does not exist or is not active, the person
  sees the selection screen with a message explaining that the country is not available.
- Changing the country after starting the wizard discards the data entered for the
  previous country, after the person confirms it.

### Acceptance criteria

Scenario: Countries available
  Given Colombia and Chile are active and published in Strapi
  When I open the application without a country
  Then I see the country selection screen with Colombia and Chile, in the configured order

Scenario: Country selection
  Given I am on the country selection screen
  When I select Chile
  Then I move on to the data form
  And the form, plans and terms I see are the ones configured for Chile

Scenario: Direct link to a country
  Given I have a link to the application for Colombia
  When I open it
  Then I see the data form for Colombia without going through the selection screen

Scenario: Country not available
  Given the link points to a country that is not active in Strapi
  When I open it
  Then I see the country selection screen
  And I see a message explaining that the country is not available

Scenario: Change of country
  Given I entered data in the form for Colombia
  When I choose to change the country to Chile
  Then I am asked to confirm that my data will be discarded
  And if I confirm, I see the empty form for Chile

Scenario: Keyboard selection
  Given I am on the country selection screen
  When I use only the keyboard
  Then I can move between the countries, select one and continue
</pasted_content id="512d">

## US-00 – Country selection

### Story

As a person interested in insuring my car, I want to choose the country where I want
to buy the insurance, so that the form, plans, prices and terms I see apply to my country.

### Context

The same application sells car insurance in Colombia and Chile. Everything the person
sees in the following steps (form fields, plans, currency, terms and conditions) depends
on the country, so the country must be known before the wizard starts. The business team
wants to manage the available countries from Strapi, including their name and flag or
icon, so that a new country can be offered without changing code.

### Business rules

- The available countries are configured in Strapi with: name, code, icon, order and
  active status.
- Only published and active countries are shown, in the configured order.
- Only one country can be selected.
- The selected country is reflected in the address, so a shared link opens the
  application directly in that country, without going through the selection screen.
- If the address contains a country that does not exist or is not active, the person
  sees the selection screen with a message explaining that the country is not available.
- Changing the country after starting the wizard discards the data entered for the
  previous country, after the person confirms it.

### Acceptance criteria

```gherkin
Scenario: Countries available
  Given Colombia and Chile are active and published in Strapi
  When I open the application without a country
  Then I see the country selection screen with Colombia and Chile, in the configured order

Scenario: Country selection
  Given I am on the country selection screen
  When I select Chile
  Then I move on to the data form
  And the form, plans and terms I see are the ones configured for Chile

Scenario: Direct link to a country
  Given I have a link to the application for Colombia
  When I open it
  Then I see the data form for Colombia without going through the selection screen

Scenario: Country not available
  Given the link points to a country that is not active in Strapi
  When I open it
  Then I see the country selection screen
  And I see a message explaining that the country is not available

Scenario: Change of country
  Given I entered data in the form for Colombia
  When I choose to change the country to Chile
  Then I am asked to confirm that my data will be discarded
  And if I confirm, I see the empty form for Chile

Scenario: Keyboard selection
  Given I am on the country selection screen
  When I use only the keyboard
  Then I can move between the countries, select one and continue
```

   - Create a 2-4 word short name that captures the essence of the feature
   - Use action-noun format when possible (e.g., "add-user-auth", "fix-payment-bug")
   - Preserve technical terms and acronyms (OAuth2, API, JWT, etc.)
   - Keep it concise but descriptive enough to understand the feature at a glance
   - Examples:
     - "I want to add user authentication" → "user-auth"
     - "Implement OAuth2 integration for the API" → "oauth2-api-integration"
     - "Create a dashboard for analytics" → "analytics-dashboard"
     - "Fix payment processing timeout bug" → "fix-payment-timeout"

2. **Branch creation** (optional, via hook):

   If a `before_specify` hook ran successfully in the Pre-Execution Checks above, it will have created/switched to a git branch and output JSON containing `BRANCH_NAME` and `FEATURE_NUM`. Note these values for reference, but the branch name does **not** dictate the spec directory name.

   If the user explicitly provided `GIT_BRANCH_NAME`, pass it through to the hook so the branch script uses the exact value as the branch name (bypassing all prefix/suffix generation).

3. **Create the spec feature directory**:

   Specs live under the default `specs/` directory unless the user explicitly provides `SPECIFY_FEATURE_DIRECTORY`.

   **Resolution order for `SPECIFY_FEATURE_DIRECTORY`**:
   1. If the user explicitly provided `SPECIFY_FEATURE_DIRECTORY` (e.g., via environment variable, argument, or configuration), use it as-is
   2. Otherwise, auto-generate it under `specs/`:
      - Check `.specify/init-options.json` for `feature_numbering` (preferred) or `branch_numbering` (deprecated, migration only — will be removed in a future release)
      - If `"timestamp"`: prefix is `YYYYMMDD-HHMMSS` (current timestamp)
      - If `"sequential"` or absent: prefix is `NNN` (next available 3-digit number after scanning existing directories in `specs/`)
      - Construct the directory name: `<prefix>-<short-name>` (e.g., `003-user-auth` or `20260319-143022-user-auth`)
      - Set `SPECIFY_FEATURE_DIRECTORY` to `specs/<directory-name>`
      - If `branch_numbering` was used (and `feature_numbering` was absent), emit a one-line warning: "⚠️ `branch_numbering` in init-options.json is deprecated. Rename to `feature_numbering`."

   **Create the directory and spec file**:
   - Run `.specify/scripts/bash/resolve-template.sh spec-template --json` from the repository root and parse `TEMPLATE_CONTENT` as the active `spec-template`. The shared resolver composes project overrides, preset layers, and extension layers over the core template, including `append`, `prepend`, and `wrap` strategies. If it fails, stop and report the resolution error; do not continue with only one contributing template layer.
   - `mkdir -p SPECIFY_FEATURE_DIRECTORY`
   - Write `TEMPLATE_CONTENT` to `SPECIFY_FEATURE_DIRECTORY/spec.md` as the starting point. Do not copy a template file from disk instead: when a preset composes `spec-template`, no single file holds the full template.
   - Set `SPEC_FILE` to `SPECIFY_FEATURE_DIRECTORY/spec.md`
   - Persist the resolved path to `.specify/feature.json`:
     ```json
     {
       "feature_directory": "<resolved feature dir>"
     }
     ```
     Write the actual resolved directory path value (for example, `specs/003-user-auth`), not the literal string `SPECIFY_FEATURE_DIRECTORY`.
     This allows downstream commands (`/speckit-plan`, `/speckit-tasks`, etc.) to locate the feature directory without relying on git branch name conventions.

   **IMPORTANT**:
   - You must only create one feature per `/speckit-specify` invocation
   - The spec directory name and the git branch name are independent — they may be the same but that is the user's choice
   - The spec directory and file are always created by this command, never by the hook

4. Use `TEMPLATE_CONTENT` to understand required sections.

5. **IF EXISTS**: Load `.specify/memory/constitution.md` for project principles and governance constraints.

6. Follow this execution flow:
    1. Parse user description from arguments
       If empty: ERROR "No feature description provided"
    2. Extract key concepts from description
       Identify: actors, actions, data, constraints
    3. For unclear aspects:
       - Make informed guesses based on context and industry standards
       - Only mark with [NEEDS CLARIFICATION: specific question] if:
         - The choice significantly impacts feature scope or user experience
         - Multiple reasonable interpretations exist with different implications
         - No reasonable default exists
       - **LIMIT: Maximum 3 [NEEDS CLARIFICATION] markers total**
       - Prioritize clarifications by impact: scope > security/privacy > user experience > technical details
    4. Fill User Scenarios & Testing section
       If no clear user flow: ERROR "Cannot determine user scenarios"
    5. Generate Functional Requirements
       Each requirement must be testable
       Use reasonable defaults for unspecified details (document assumptions in Assumptions section)
    6. Define Success Criteria
       Create measurable, technology-agnostic outcomes
       Include both quantitative metrics (time, performance, volume) and qualitative measures (user satisfaction, task completion)
       Each criterion must be verifiable without implementation details
    7. Identify Key Entities (if data involved)
    8. Return: SUCCESS (spec ready for planning)

7. Write the specification to SPEC_FILE using the template structure, replacing placeholders with concrete details derived from the feature description (arguments) while preserving section order and headings.

8. **Specification Quality Validation**: After writing the initial spec, validate it against quality criteria:

   a. **Create Spec Quality Checklist**: Generate a checklist file at `SPECIFY_FEATURE_DIRECTORY/checklists/requirements.md` using the checklist template structure with these validation items:

      ```markdown
      # Specification Quality Checklist: [FEATURE NAME]

      **Purpose**: Validate specification completeness and quality before proceeding to planning
      **Created**: [DATE]
      **Feature**: [Link to spec.md]

      ## Content Quality

      - [ ] No implementation details (languages, frameworks, APIs)
      - [ ] Focused on user value and business needs
      - [ ] Written for non-technical stakeholders
      - [ ] All mandatory sections completed

      ## Requirement Completeness

      - [ ] No [NEEDS CLARIFICATION] markers remain
      - [ ] Requirements are testable and unambiguous
      - [ ] Success criteria are measurable
      - [ ] Success criteria are technology-agnostic (no implementation details)
      - [ ] All acceptance scenarios are defined
      - [ ] Edge cases are identified
      - [ ] Scope is clearly bounded
      - [ ] Dependencies and assumptions identified

      ## Feature Readiness

      - [ ] All functional requirements have clear acceptance criteria
      - [ ] User scenarios cover primary flows
      - [ ] Feature meets measurable outcomes defined in Success Criteria
      - [ ] No implementation details leak into specification

      ## Notes

      - Items marked incomplete require spec updates before `/speckit-clarify` or `/speckit-plan`
      ```

   b. **Run Validation Check**: Review the spec against each checklist item:
      - For each item, determine if it passes or fails
      - Document specific issues found (quote relevant spec sections)

   c. **Handle Validation Results**:

      - **If all items pass**: Mark checklist complete and proceed to the Mandatory Post-Execution Hooks section

      - **If items fail (excluding [NEEDS CLARIFICATION])**:
        1. List the failing items and specific issues
        2. Update the spec to address each issue
        3. Re-run validation until all items pass (max 3 iterations)
        4. If still failing after 3 iterations, document remaining issues in checklist notes and warn user

      - **If [NEEDS CLARIFICATION] markers remain**:
        1. Extract all [NEEDS CLARIFICATION: ...] markers from the spec
        2. **LIMIT CHECK**: If more than 3 markers exist, keep only the 3 most critical (by scope/security/UX impact) and make informed guesses for the rest
        3. For each clarification needed (max 3), present options to user in this format:

           ```markdown
           ## Question [N]: [Topic]

           **Context**: [Quote relevant spec section]

           **What we need to know**: [Specific question from NEEDS CLARIFICATION marker]

           **Suggested Answers**:

           | Option | Answer | Implications |
           |--------|--------|--------------|
           | A      | [First suggested answer] | [What this means for the feature] |
           | B      | [Second suggested answer] | [What this means for the feature] |
           | C      | [Third suggested answer] | [What this means for the feature] |
           | Custom | Provide your own answer | [Explain how to provide custom input] |

           **Your choice**: _[Wait for user response]_
           ```

        4. **CRITICAL - Table Formatting**: Ensure markdown tables are properly formatted:
           - Use consistent spacing with pipes aligned
           - Each cell should have spaces around content: `| Content |` not `|Content|`
           - Header separator must have at least 3 dashes: `|--------|`
           - Test that the table renders correctly in markdown preview
        5. Number questions sequentially (Q1, Q2, Q3 - max 3 total)
        6. Present all questions together before waiting for responses
        7. Wait for user to respond with their choices for all questions (e.g., "Q1: A, Q2: Custom - [details], Q3: B")
        8. Update the spec by replacing each [NEEDS CLARIFICATION] marker with the user's selected or provided answer
        9. Re-run validation after all clarifications are resolved

   d. **Update Checklist**: After each validation iteration, update the checklist file with current pass/fail status

**You MUST complete this section before reporting completion to the user.**

Check if `.specify/extensions.yml` exists in the project root.

- For each executable hook, output the following based on its `optional` flag:

    ```
    ## Extension Hooks

    **Automatic Hook**: {extension}
    Executing: `/{command}`
    EXECUTE_COMMAND: {command}
    ```
    After emitting the block above you MUST actually invoke the hook and wait for it to finish before continuing. Run it the same way you would run the command yourself in this agent/session (the invocation may differ from the literal `{command}` id shown above, e.g. a skills-mode agent runs it as `/skill:speckit-...` or `$speckit-...`). Emitting the block alone does not run the hook.
  - **Optional hook** (`optional: true`):
    ```
    ## Extension Hooks

    **Optional Hook**: {extension}
    Command: `/{command}`
    Description: {description}

    Prompt: {prompt}
    To execute: `/{command}`
    ```

## Completion Report

Report completion to the user with:
- `SPECIFY_FEATURE_DIRECTORY` — the feature directory path
- `SPEC_FILE` — the spec file path
- Checklist results summary
- Readiness for the next phase (`/speckit-clarify` or `/speckit-plan`)

**NOTE:** Branch creation is handled by the `before_specify` hook (git extension). Spec directory and file creation are always handled by this core command.

## Quick Guidelines

- Focus on **WHAT** users need and **WHY**.
- Avoid HOW to implement (no tech stack, APIs, code structure).
- Written for business stakeholders, not developers.
- DO NOT create any checklists that are embedded in the spec. That will be a separate command.

### Section Requirements

- **Mandatory sections**: Must be completed for every feature
- **Optional sections**: Include only when relevant to the feature
- When a section doesn't apply, remove it entirely (don't leave as "N/A")

### For AI Generation

When creating this spec from a user prompt:

1. **Make informed guesses**: Use context, industry standards, and common patterns to fill gaps
2. **Document assumptions**: Record reasonable defaults in the Assumptions section
3. **Limit clarifications**: Maximum 3 [NEEDS CLARIFICATION] markers - use only for critical decisions that:
   - Significantly impact feature scope or user experience
   - Have multiple reasonable interpretations with different implications
   - Lack any reasonable default
4. **Prioritize clarifications**: scope > security/privacy > user experience > technical details
5. **Think like a tester**: Every vague requirement should fail the "testable and unambiguous" checklist item
6. **Common areas needing clarification** (only if no reasonable default exists):
   - Feature scope and boundaries (include/exclude specific use cases)
   - User types and permissions (if multiple conflicting interpretations possible)
   - Security/compliance requirements (when legally/financially significant)

**Examples of reasonable defaults** (don't ask about these):

- Data retention: Industry-standard practices for the domain
- Performance targets: Standard web/mobile app expectations unless specified
- Error handling: User-friendly messages with appropriate fallbacks
- Authentication method: Standard session-based or OAuth2 for web apps
- Integration patterns: Use project-appropriate patterns (REST/GraphQL for web services, function calls for libraries, CLI args for tools, etc.)

### Success Criteria Guidelines

Success criteria must be:

1. **Measurable**: Include specific metrics (time, percentage, count, rate)
2. **Technology-agnostic**: No mention of frameworks, languages, databases, or tools
3. **User-focused**: Describe outcomes from user/business perspective, not system internals
4. **Verifiable**: Can be tested/validated without knowing implementation details

**Good examples**:

- "Users can complete checkout in under 3 minutes"
- "System supports 10,000 concurrent users"
- "95% of searches return results in under 1 second"
- "Task completion rate improves by 40%"

**Bad examples** (implementation-focused):

- "API response time is under 200ms" (too technical, use "Users see results instantly")
- "Database can handle 1000 TPS" (implementation detail, use user-facing metric)
- "React components render efficiently" (framework-specific)
- "Redis cache hit rate above 80%" (technology-specific)

- [ ] Specification written to `SPEC_FILE` and validated against quality checklist
- [ ] Extension hooks dispatched or skipped according to the rules in Mandatory Post-Execution Hooks above
- [ ] Completion reported to user with feature directory, spec file path, and checklist results

# Feature Specification: US-00 – Country selection

**Feature Branch**: `001-us-00-country-selection`

**Created**: 2026-11-22

**Status**: Draft

**Input**: User story [US-00](../../docs/user-stories/US-00.md) (verbatim business story — source of truth). Architecture: [ADR 0001](../../docs/adr/0001-multi-country-content-strategy.md).

## User Scenarios & Testing *(mandatory)*

### User Story 1 - Choose a country and enter the wizard (Priority: P1)

A person opens the application without a country and picks Colombia or Chile from the countries the business has made available. From then on, everything they see belongs to that country.

**Why this priority**: Nothing else in the wizard can be shown until the country is known; it is the entry point of every quote.

**Independent Test**: With Colombia and Chile active and published, open the application root, pick a country and check that the first wizard step opens in that country's context.

**Acceptance Scenarios**:

1. **Given** Colombia and Chile are active and published, **When** I open the application without a country, **Then** I see the selection screen with Colombia and Chile, each with its name and icon, in the configured order.
2. **Given** I am on the selection screen, **When** I select Chile, **Then** I move on to the data form for Chile, and the address shows Chile.
3. **Given** I am on the selection screen, **When** I use only the keyboard, **Then** I can move between the countries, select one and continue.

---

### User Story 2 - Open the application directly in a country (Priority: P1)

# Project Context & Rules

Always read and follow `.specify/memory/constitution.md` before planning, writing code, or running commands.
The full agentic flow (steps, gates, agents) is described in `FLOW.md`.

## Repository Structure
- `cms/`: Headless CMS built with Strapi 5 (TypeScript, SQLite). Content types, APIs, seed, permissions.
- `frontend/`: Angular 22 app (TypeScript, ESLint), Vitest unit tests next to the code, Playwright e2e in `frontend/e2e/`.
- `docs/user-stories/`: Functional user stories pasted verbatim by the human (`US-XX.md`). Never edited by AI.
- `docs/adr/`: Architecture Decision Records (MADR), `NNNN-<slug>.md`.
- `specs/NNN-us-XX-<slug>/`: `spec.md`, `plan.md`, `tasks.md`, `analysis.md`, `review.md` per user story (Spec Kit).
- `.claude/agents/`: subagent definitions. `.claude/skills/`: skills.
- `ai-logs/`: exported agent sessions. Never edit.

## Verification Commands
- **Frontend (lint + typecheck + unit tests):** `npm --prefix frontend run verify`
- **Frontend build:** `npm --prefix frontend run build`
- **Frontend e2e (Playwright):** `npm --prefix frontend run e2e`
- **CMS build / typecheck:** `npm --prefix cms run build`
- **CMS dev server:** `npm --prefix cms run develop`
- **Full stack:** `docker compose up --build`

## Stack Rules (all agents)
- **Angular:** standalone components only, no NgModules; signals for state; built-in control flow (`@if`, `@for`, `@switch`); typed forms; no `any`. Details: `angular-conventions` skill.
- **Strapi:** schemas defined in code; Public role gets only `find`/`findOne` on what the wizard reads. Details: `strapi-conventions` skill.
- **Security:** no Strapi token of any kind in the frontend; the browser calls only relative `/api/...` URLs (proxied by nginx / `proxy.conf.json`).
- **Accessibility:** every field has a visible label; the wizard is fully keyboard-operable; works on mobile and desktop.
- **Data:** fictitious data only. No real personal data, documents, plates or credentials anywhere in the repo.

## Plan Phase Additions (Gate 2)
`plan.md` must also contain, when applicable:
- **E2E candidates:** list only critical flows that deserve an e2e test, each with a one-line justification. The human marks each one **Approved** or **Rejected** at Gate 2. The `e2e-tester` agent runs only for approved candidates.
- **Design options:** for every client-facing view, 2–3 design options based on the `ui-ux-guidelines` skill, with a recommendation. The human picks one at Gate 2.
- **ADRs:** every architectural decision gets an ADR in `docs/adr/` (context, alternatives, consequences), linked from `plan.md`.
- **Revisions:** when the human rejects or corrects the plan at Gate 2, append an entry to a `## Revisions` section at the end of `plan.md`: date, what the human asked to change, and what changed. Never delete entries.

## Traceability
- The user story ID `US-XX` appears in: spec folder name, spec header, each task line, ADR "Related" field, test names (`describe('US-XX · FR-XXX …')`), and commit footer `Refs: US-XX`.
- Requirements in `spec.md` are numbered `FR-XXX`; tasks and tests reference them.
- Gate approvals are recorded in the artifact header: `**Status**: Approved (Gate 1|2) — <date>`. Gate 3 is recorded as the last line of `review.md`: `Gate 3: Approved — <date>`.
- Human corrections: Gate 1 in `spec.md` › Clarifications, Gate 2 in `plan.md` › Revisions, Gate 3 as new tasks in `tasks.md`.

## Security & Workflow Hygiene
- **NEVER** read, print, or commit `cms/.env` or any `.env` file (only read `.env.example` when checking required environment variables).
- The Strapi schema (`cms/src/api/`) is the source of truth for API contracts; Angular models in `frontend/src/app/features/*/data/` must match it. A schema change updates the models in the same commit.
- Never edit `.specify/templates/`, `.specify/scripts/`, `.claude/skills/speckit-*` or the constitution unless the human explicitly asks.

# Feature Specification: US-00 – Country selection

**Feature Branch**: `001-us-00-country-selection`

**Created**: 2026-11-22

**Status**: Draft

**Input**: User story [US-00](../../docs/user-stories/US-00.md) (verbatim business story — source of truth). Architecture: [ADR 0001](../../docs/adr/0001-multi-country-content-strategy.md).

## User Scenarios & Testing *(mandatory)*

### User Story 1 - Choose a country and enter the wizard (Priority: P1)

A person opens the application without a country and picks Colombia or Chile from the countries the business has made available. From then on, everything they see belongs to that country.

**Why this priority**: Nothing else in the wizard can be shown until the country is known; it is the entry point of every quote.

**Independent Test**: With Colombia and Chile active and published, open the application root, pick a country and check that the first wizard step opens in that country's context.

**Acceptance Scenarios**:

1. **Given** Colombia and Chile are active and published, **When** I open the application without a country, **Then** I see the selection screen with Colombia and Chile, each with its name and icon, in the configured order.
2. **Given** I am on the selection screen, **When** I select Chile, **Then** I move on to the data form for Chile, and the address shows Chile.
3. **Given** I am on the selection screen, **When** I use only the keyboard, **Then** I can move between the countries, select one and continue.

---

### User Story 2 - Open the application directly in a country (Priority: P1)

A person receives a link for a country and lands directly in that country's wizard. If the link points to a country that isn't offered, they are told so and can pick an available one.

**Why this priority**: Shared links are how marketing and support send people to the right country; a broken link must never be a dead end.

**Independent Test**: Open a Colombia link and check the selection screen is skipped; open a link for an unknown or inactive country and check the selection screen shows the "not available" message.

**Acceptance Scenarios**:

1. **Given** I have a link to the application for Colombia, **When** I open it, **Then** I see the data form for Colombia without going through the selection screen.
2. **Given** the link points to a country that does not exist, is not active, or is not published, **When** I open it, **Then** I see the selection screen and a message explaining that the country is not available.

---

### User Story 3 - Change the country after starting (Priority: P2)

A person who already entered data for one country decides to quote in another one. They are warned that their data will be discarded and decide whether to continue.

**Why this priority**: Less frequent than the first entry, but losing data without warning would break trust.

**Independent Test**: Enter data in the Colombia form, choose to change to Chile, cancel (data kept), then confirm (empty Chile form).

**Acceptance Scenarios**:

1. **Given** I entered data in the form for Colombia, **When** I choose to change the country to Chile, **Then** I am asked to confirm that my data will be discarded.
2. **Given** I am asked to confirm, **When** I confirm, **Then** I see the empty form for Chile and the Colombia data is gone.
3. **Given** I am asked to confirm, **When** I cancel, **Then** I stay in Colombia with my data untouched.
4. **Given** I have not entered any data yet, **When** I choose to change the country, **Then** I go to the selection screen without a confirmation.

---

### Edge Cases

- **No countries available** (none active and published, or the content service fails): the selection screen shows a clear message instead of an empty list, and a retry action if the service failed.
- **Only one country available**: the selection screen is still shown; the person selects it explicitly.
- **Country without an icon**: it is shown with its name only; the layout does not break.
- **Country deactivated while the person is in the wizard**: on the next reload, the person lands on the selection screen with the "not available" message.
- **Country code in the address with different letter case** (e.g. `CO` vs `co`): treated as the same country.

## Requirements *(mandatory)*

### Functional Requirements

- **FR-001**: The business team MUST be able to configure each country with name, code, icon, order and active status, without code changes.
- **FR-002**: The selection screen MUST show only countries that are both published and active, sorted by their configured order.
- **FR-003**: The person MUST be able to select exactly one country.
- **FR-004**: After selection, the application MUST open the first wizard step (data form) for that country.
- **FR-005**: The selected country MUST be part of the address, so that opening that address later shows that country's wizard directly, without the selection screen.
- **FR-006**: An address with a country that does not exist, is not active or is not published MUST show the selection screen with a message explaining that the country is not available.
- **FR-007**: Changing the country after data was entered MUST ask for confirmation; confirming discards the previous country's data, cancelling keeps it.
- **FR-008**: Every country-dependent content shown in later steps (form, plans, currency, terms) MUST come from the selected country.
- **FR-009**: The selection screen MUST be fully operable with the keyboard, and each country MUST have an accessible name.
- **FR-010**: The selection screen MUST show loading, empty and error states (see Edge Cases).

### Key Entities

- **Country**: a market where insurance is sold. Attributes in this story: name, code (also used in the address), icon, order, active status, publication status. Further attributes (currency, number format, legal age, terms) are defined in ADR 0001 and used by later stories.

## Success Criteria *(mandatory)*

### Measurable Outcomes

- **SC-001**: A person reaches the data form of their country in at most 2 actions from the application root.
- **SC-002**: 100% of addresses with an available country open that country directly; 100% of addresses with an unavailable country show the "not available" message.
- **SC-003**: A new country published and activated by the business team appears on the selection screen after a reload, with no deployment.
- **SC-004**: The whole selection, including changing country, can be completed using only the keyboard.

## Assumptions

- Copy is in Spanish for both countries; the "not available" and "no countries" messages are fixed application texts (an unavailable country has no content to take them from).
- "Data form" is the step delivered by US-01. Until US-01 lands, the destination of FR-004 is the first wizard step showing the selected country (name and icon).
- Data entered for a country is kept only in the browser session, per country (ADR 0001).

## Conflicts with ADR 0001 *(to resolve at Gate 2)*

- **New Country attributes:** the story adds `icon`, `order` and `active`; ADR 0001 has none of them.
- **Two availability switches:** ADR 0001 uses publish/unpublish as the on/off switch; the story requires *published and active*. Both will apply (FR-002, FR-006).
- **Sort order:** ADR 0001 sorts countries by name; the story requires the configured order (FR-002).
- **Change of country:** ADR 0001 says changing country restarts the wizard; the story adds a confirmation before discarding data (FR-007).
- **Preselected country:** ADR 0001 preselects the last visited country on the selection screen; the story does not mention it.

# Feature Specification: US-00 – Country selection

**Feature Branch**: `001-us-00-country-selection`

**Created**: 2026-11-22

**Status**: Draft

**Input**: User story [US-00](../../docs/user-stories/US-00.md) (verbatim business story — source of truth). Architecture: [ADR 0001](../../docs/adr/0001-multi-country-content-strategy.md).

## Clarifications

### Session 2026-11-22

- Q: On the selection screen, does picking a country go straight to the form, or pick it and then press "Continue"? → A: Select, then Continue. The countries are a single-choice group; a "Continue" button, disabled until a country is chosen, opens the form.

## User Scenarios & Testing *(mandatory)*

### User Story 1 - Choose a country and enter the wizard (Priority: P1)

A person opens the application without a country and picks Colombia or Chile from the countries the business has made available. From then on, everything they see belongs to that country.

**Why this priority**: Nothing else in the wizard can be shown until the country is known; it is the entry point of every quote.

**Independent Test**: With Colombia and Chile active and published, open the application root, pick a country and check that the first wizard step opens in that country's context.

**Acceptance Scenarios**:

1. **Given** Colombia and Chile are active and published, **When** I open the application without a country, **Then** I see the selection screen with Colombia and Chile, each with its name and icon, in the configured order.
2. **Given** I am on the selection screen, **When** I select Chile and press "Continue", **Then** I move on to the data form for Chile, and the address shows Chile.
4. **Given** I am on the selection screen and no country is selected, **When** I look at "Continue", **Then** it is disabled.
3. **Given** I am on the selection screen, **When** I use only the keyboard, **Then** I can move between the countries, select one and continue.

---

### User Story 2 - Open the application directly in a country (Priority: P1)

A person receives a link for a country and lands directly in that country's wizard. If the link points to a country that isn't offered, they are told so and can pick an available one.

**Why this priority**: Shared links are how marketing and support send people to the right country; a broken link must never be a dead end.

**Independent Test**: Open a Colombia link and check the selection screen is skipped; open a link for an unknown or inactive country and check the selection screen shows the "not available" message.

**Acceptance Scenarios**:

1. **Given** I have a link to the application for Colombia, **When** I open it, **Then** I see the data form for Colombia without going through the selection screen.
2. **Given** the link points to a country that does not exist, is not active, or is not published, **When** I open it, **Then** I see the selection screen and a message explaining that the country is not available.

---

### User Story 3 - Change the country after starting (Priority: P2)

A person who already entered data for one country decides to quote in another one. They are warned that their data will be discarded and decide whether to continue.

**Why this priority**: Less frequent than the first entry, but losing data without warning would break trust.

**Independent Test**: Enter data in the Colombia form, choose to change to Chile, cancel (data kept), then confirm (empty Chile form).

**Acceptance Scenarios**:

1. **Given** I entered data in the form for Colombia, **When** I choose to change the country to Chile, **Then** I am asked to confirm that my data will be discarded.
2. **Given** I am asked to confirm, **When** I confirm, **Then** I see the empty form for Chile and the Colombia data is gone.
3. **Given** I am asked to confirm, **When** I cancel, **Then** I stay in Colombia with my data untouched.
4. **Given** I have not entered any data yet, **When** I choose to change the country, **Then** I go to the selection screen without a confirmation.

---

### Edge Cases

- **No countries available** (none active and published, or the content service fails): the selection screen shows a clear message instead of an empty list, and a retry action if the service failed.
- **Only one country available**: the selection screen is still shown; the person selects it explicitly.
- **Country without an icon**: it is shown with its name only; the layout does not break.
- **Country deactivated while the person is in the wizard**: on the next reload, the person lands on the selection screen with the "not available" message.
- **Country code in the address with different letter case** (e.g. `CO` vs `co`): treated as the same country.

## Requirements *(mandatory)*

### Functional Requirements

- **FR-001**: The business team MUST be able to configure each country with name, code, icon, order and active status, without code changes.
- **FR-002**: The selection screen MUST show only countries that are both published and active, sorted by their configured order.
- **FR-003**: The person MUST be able to select exactly one country from a single-choice group; selecting does not navigate by itself.
- **FR-004**: A "Continue" action, disabled until a country is selected, MUST open the first wizard step (data form) for the selected country.
- **FR-005**: The selected country MUST be part of the address, so that opening that address later shows that country's wizard directly, without the selection screen.
- **FR-006**: An address with a country that does not exist, is not active or is not published MUST show the selection screen with a message explaining that the country is not available.
- **FR-007**: Changing the country after data was entered MUST ask for confirmation; confirming discards the previous country's data, cancelling keeps it.
- **FR-008**: Every country-dependent content shown in later steps (form, plans, currency, terms) MUST come from the selected country.
- **FR-009**: The selection screen MUST be fully operable with the keyboard, and each country MUST have an accessible name.
- **FR-010**: The selection screen MUST show loading, empty and error states (see Edge Cases).

### Key Entities

- **Country**: a market where insurance is sold. Attributes in this story: name, code (also used in the address), icon, order, active status, publication status. Further attributes (currency, number format, legal age, terms) are defined in ADR 0001 and used by later stories.

## Success Criteria *(mandatory)*

### Measurable Outcomes

- **SC-001**: A person reaches the data form of their country in at most 2 actions from the application root.
- **SC-002**: 100% of addresses with an available country open that country directly; 100% of addresses with an unavailable country show the "not available" message.
- **SC-003**: A new country published and activated by the business team appears on the selection screen after a reload, with no deployment.
- **SC-004**: The whole selection, including changing country, can be completed using only the keyboard.

## Assumptions

- Copy is in Spanish for both countries; the "not available" and "no countries" messages are fixed application texts (an unavailable country has no content to take them from).
- "Data form" is the step delivered by US-01. Until US-01 lands, the destination of FR-004 is the first wizard step showing the selected country (name and icon).
- Data entered for a country is kept only in the browser session, per country (ADR 0001).

## Conflicts with ADR 0001 *(to resolve at Gate 2)*

- **New Country attributes:** the story adds `icon`, `order` and `active`; ADR 0001 has none of them.
- **Two availability switches:** ADR 0001 uses publish/unpublish as the on/off switch; the story requires *published and active*. Both will apply (FR-002, FR-006).
- **Sort order:** ADR 0001 sorts countries by name; the story requires the configured order (FR-002).
- **Change of country:** ADR 0001 says changing country restarts the wizard; the story adds a confirmation before discarding data (FR-007).
- **Preselected country:** ADR 0001 preselects the last visited country on the selection screen; the story does not mention it.

- **Country without an icon**: it is shown with its name only; the layout does not break.

- **FR-002**: The selection screen MUST show only countries that are both published and active, sorted by their configured order.
- **FR-003**: The person MUST be able to select exactly one country from a single-choice group; selecting does not navigate by itself.
- **FR-004**: A "Continue" action, disabled until a country is selected, MUST open the first wizard step (data form) for the selected country.
- **FR-011**: When the person returns to the selection screen, the country last visited in the same browser session MUST start selected if it is still available; otherwise no country is selected.

# Feature Specification: US-00 – Country selection

**Feature Branch**: `001-us-00-country-selection`

**Created**: 2026-11-22

**Status**: Draft

**Input**: User story [US-00](../../docs/user-stories/US-00.md) (verbatim business story — source of truth). Architecture: [ADR 0001](../../docs/adr/0001-multi-country-content-strategy.md).

## Clarifications

### Session 2026-11-22

- Q: On the selection screen, does picking a country go straight to the form, or pick it and then press "Continue"? → A: Select, then Continue. The countries are a single-choice group; a "Continue" button, disabled until a country is chosen, opens the form.
- Q: When someone returns to the selection screen, is the country they last visited in this session already selected? → A: Yes. If a country was visited in this browser session and is still available, it starts selected and "Continue" is enabled; otherwise nothing is selected.
- Q: Where does the person choose to change the country inside the wizard? → A: A header control on every wizard step shows the active country (icon + name) with a "Cambiar país" button; it asks for confirmation if data was entered, then opens the selection screen.

## User Scenarios & Testing *(mandatory)*

### User Story 1 - Choose a country and enter the wizard (Priority: P1)

A person opens the application without a country and picks Colombia or Chile from the countries the business has made available. From then on, everything they see belongs to that country.

**Why this priority**: Nothing else in the wizard can be shown until the country is known; it is the entry point of every quote.

**Independent Test**: With Colombia and Chile active and published, open the application root, pick a country and check that the first wizard step opens in that country's context.

**Acceptance Scenarios**:

1. **Given** Colombia and Chile are active and published, **When** I open the application without a country, **Then** I see the selection screen with Colombia and Chile, each with its name and icon, in the configured order.
2. **Given** I am on the selection screen, **When** I select Chile and press "Continue", **Then** I move on to the data form for Chile, and the address shows Chile.
4. **Given** I am on the selection screen and no country is selected, **When** I look at "Continue", **Then** it is disabled.
3. **Given** I am on the selection screen, **When** I use only the keyboard, **Then** I can move between the countries, select one and continue.

---

### User Story 2 - Open the application directly in a country (Priority: P1)

A person receives a link for a country and lands directly in that country's wizard. If the link points to a country that isn't offered, they are told so and can pick an available one.

**Why this priority**: Shared links are how marketing and support send people to the right country; a broken link must never be a dead end.

**Independent Test**: Open a Colombia link and check the selection screen is skipped; open a link for an unknown or inactive country and check the selection screen shows the "not available" message.

**Acceptance Scenarios**:

1. **Given** I have a link to the application for Colombia, **When** I open it, **Then** I see the data form for Colombia without going through the selection screen.
2. **Given** the link points to a country that does not exist, is not active, or is not published, **When** I open it, **Then** I see the selection screen and a message explaining that the country is not available.

---

### User Story 3 - Change the country after starting (Priority: P2)

A person who already entered data for one country decides to quote in another one. They are warned that their data will be discarded and decide whether to continue.

**Why this priority**: Less frequent than the first entry, but losing data without warning would break trust.

**Independent Test**: Enter data in the Colombia form, choose to change to Chile, cancel (data kept), then confirm (empty Chile form).

**Acceptance Scenarios**:

1. **Given** I entered data in the form for Colombia, **When** I choose to change the country to Chile, **Then** I am asked to confirm that my data will be discarded.
2. **Given** I am asked to confirm, **When** I confirm, **Then** I see the empty form for Chile and the Colombia data is gone.
3. **Given** I am asked to confirm, **When** I cancel, **Then** I stay in Colombia with my data untouched.
4. **Given** I have not entered any data yet, **When** I choose to change the country, **Then** I go to the selection screen without a confirmation.

---

### Edge Cases

- **No countries available** (none active and published, or the content service fails): the selection screen shows a clear message instead of an empty list, and a retry action if the service failed.
- **Only one country available**: the selection screen is still shown; the person selects it explicitly.
- **Country without an icon**: it is shown with its name only; the layout does not break.
- **Country deactivated while the person is in the wizard**: on the next reload, the person lands on the selection screen with the "not available" message.
- **Country code in the address with different letter case** (e.g. `CO` vs `co`): treated as the same country.

## Requirements *(mandatory)*

### Functional Requirements

- **FR-001**: The business team MUST be able to configure each country with name, code, icon, order and active status, without code changes.
- **FR-002**: The selection screen MUST show only countries that are both published and active, sorted by their configured order.
- **FR-003**: The person MUST be able to select exactly one country from a single-choice group; selecting does not navigate by itself.
- **FR-004**: A "Continue" action, disabled until a country is selected, MUST open the first wizard step (data form) for the selected country.
- **FR-011**: When the person returns to the selection screen, the country last visited in the same browser session MUST start selected if it is still available; otherwise no country is selected.
- **FR-005**: The selected country MUST be part of the address, so that opening that address later shows that country's wizard directly, without the selection screen.
- **FR-006**: An address with a country that does not exist, is not active or is not published MUST show the selection screen with a message explaining that the country is not available.
- **FR-007**: Every wizard step MUST show the active country (icon and name) and a "Cambiar país" control. Using it after data was entered MUST ask for confirmation; confirming discards that country's data and opens the selection screen, cancelling keeps the person where they were with their data.
- **FR-008**: Every country-dependent content shown in later steps (form, plans, currency, terms) MUST come from the selected country.
- **FR-009**: The selection screen MUST be fully operable with the keyboard, and each country MUST have an accessible name.
- **FR-010**: The selection screen MUST show loading, empty and error states (see Edge Cases).

### Key Entities

- **Country**: a market where insurance is sold. Attributes in this story: name, code (also used in the address), icon, order, active status, publication status. Further attributes (currency, number format, legal age, terms) are defined in ADR 0001 and used by later stories.

- **SC-001**: A person reaches the data form of their country in at most 2 actions from the application root.
- **SC-002**: 100% of addresses with an available country open that country directly; 100% of addresses with an unavailable country show the "not available" message.

- **SC-004**: The whole selection, including changing country, can be completed using only the keyboard.

## Assumptions

- Copy is in Spanish for both countries; the "not available" and "no countries" messages are fixed application texts (an unavailable country has no content to take them from).
- "Data form" is the step delivered by US-01. Until US-01 lands, the destination of FR-004 is the first wizard step showing the selected country (name and icon).

- **Preselected country:** ADR 0001 preselects the last visited country; the story did not mention it. Kept (Clarifications, FR-011).
